claims.statement: Many more identical and allied plant forms migrated from north to south during the Glacial period than in the reverse direction, because the greater land area of the north and the larger populations there had made northern forms more advanced and dominant through natural selection and competition.
claims.quote: I suspect that this preponderant migration from north to south is due to the greater extent of land in the north, and to the northern forms having existed in their own homes in greater numbers, and having consequently been advanced through natural selection and competition to a higher stage of perfection or dominating power, than the southern forms.
claims.chapter: Ch. XI: Geographical Distribution

claims.label: Northern species naturalise far more often in the south than the reverse
claims.statement: At the present day many European species have become naturalised and partly displaced the natives in La Plata and to a lesser degree in Australia, whereas extremely few southern-hemisphere species have become naturalised anywhere in Europe.
claims.quote: Just in the same manner as we see at the present day, that very many European productions cover the ground in La Plata, and in a lesser degree in Australia, and have to a certain extent beaten the natives; whereas extremely few southern forms have become naturalised in any part of Europe,
claims.chapter: Ch. XI: Geographical Distribution

test_contract.expected_observation: Using World Checklist of Vascular Plants native and introduced distribution records by TDWG level-3 unit: A_LP = number of species native in Europe (TDWG level-1 region 1) and not native in La Plata that are recorded as introduced in La Plata (units AGE Argentina Northeast and URU Uruguay); B_LP = number of species native in La Plata and not native in Europe that are recorded as introduced in any European unit; likewise A_AU and B_AU for Australia (TDWG level-2 region 50: WAU, NTA, SOA, QLD, NSW, VIC, TAS). Supports if A_LP >= 5 * B_LP and A_AU >= 5 * B_AU.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Refutes if A_LP < 2 * B_LP or A_AU < 2 * B_AU (no strong asymmetry, or reversed). Otherwise mixed. The secondary clause 'in a lesser degree in Australia' is evaluated as A_LP > A_AU and reported, but is not part of the verdict rule because absolute counts now depend on two centuries of differing colonisation history.
test_contract.inference_method: analysis.py reads the WCVP distribution table for accepted species, defines Europe as TDWG level-1 region 1, La Plata as level-3 units AGE (Argentina Northeast) + URU (Uruguay), and Australia as level-2 region 50. A_LP is the number of species native in Europe, not native in La Plata, and flagged introduced in La Plata; B_LP is the number native in La Plata, not native in Europe, and flagged introduced in any European unit; A_AU and B_AU likewise for Australia. The pre-registered rule compares A/B ratios with thresholds 5 (supports) and 2 (refutes). Two sensitivity analyses are reported but do not enter the verdict: a wider La Plata (AGE, AGW, AGS, URU, PAR) and a restriction of each source pool to species whose entire native range lies in one TDWG continent (Europe, South America, Australasia).

claims.label: Distinct southern genera spread from a once-vegetated Antarctica before the Glacial period
claims.statement: Distinct species of genera confined to the southern hemisphere spread in radiating lines from the antarctic lands, which supported a peculiar flora during a warmer period before the Glacial period, reaching southern America, Australia and New Zealand by occasional transport and former islands.
claims.quote: I am inclined to look in the southern, as in the northern hemisphere, to a former and warmer period, before the commencement of the Glacial period, when the antarctic lands, now covered with ice, supported a highly peculiar and isolated flora.
claims.chapter: Ch. XI: Geographical Distribution

claims.label: Fresh-water species range widely and allied species occur worldwide
claims.statement: Despite being separated by land and sea barriers, many fresh-water species of quite different classes have enormous ranges, and allied fresh-water species prevail throughout the world.
claims.quote: Not only have many fresh-water species, belonging to quite different classes, an enormous range, but allied species prevail in a remarkable manner throughout the world.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

test_contract.expected_observation: Pre-registered: for every family in the fixed fresh-water and terrestrial lists, GBIF occurrence facets give the set of species and genera recorded (>= 3 records) on each of the six inhabited continents. Per class, compute P_sp = proportion of species recorded on >= 3 continents and P_gen = proportion of genera recorded on >= 3 continents, separately for the fresh-water and the terrestrial family set. SUPPORTS if in all three classes P_sp(fresh-water) > P_sp(terrestrial) AND P_gen(fresh-water) > P_gen(terrestrial), and the pooled species-level continent counts differ in the fresh-water direction (one-sided Mann-Whitney, p < 0.001).
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Pre-registered: REFUTES if, in at least two of the three classes, P_sp(fresh-water) <= P_sp(terrestrial) or P_gen(fresh-water) <= P_gen(terrestrial). Any other outcome is MIXED. A class with fewer than 200 species in either habitat set is dropped; with fewer than two classes remaining the result is inconclusive (underpowered).
test_contract.inference_method: Each pre-registered family was resolved to a GBIF backbone key and, for each of six continents, the occurrence API returned facet counts of speciesKey and genusKey (coordinates present, no geospatial issue, PRESENT, 1900-2026, fossil/living specimens excluded); a species or genus was scored present on a continent with >= 3 records. Per class and habitat set the proportion of species (P_sp) and of genera (P_gen) recorded on >= 3 continents was computed and the fresh-water and terrestrial sets compared; continents-per-species distributions were compared with one-sided Mann-Whitney tests per class and pooled.

claims.label: Fresh-water fish species are not shared between distant continents
claims.statement: The same species of fresh-water fish never occur in the fresh waters of distant continents, although within a continent fish species often range widely and irregularly, different river systems sharing some species but not others.
claims.quote: In regard to fish, I believe that the same species never occur in the fresh waters of distant continents. But on the same continent the species often range widely and almost capriciously; for two river-systems will have some fish in common and some different.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

test_contract.expected_observation: Among FishBase species flagged as fresh-water only (Fresh = 1, Brack = 0, Saltwater = 0) and not anadromous, catadromous, amphidromous or oceanodromous, zero species have 'native' or 'endemic' country status (FishBase country table) in at least one country on each side of any ocean-separated continent pair. Ocean-separated pairs are all pairs among {Eurasia (Europe + Asia), Africa, North America (incl. Central America and the Caribbean), South America, Oceania (Australia + New Guinea + Pacific)} except Eurasia-Africa and North America-South America, which are joined by land.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Five or more such species have native status in >= 2 countries on each side of an ocean-separated pair (robust counterexamples, not single-country errors): refutes. Between 1 and 4 robust species, or only single-country cases: mixed. The share of strictly fresh-water species that are shared across an ocean is reported to distinguish 'never' from 'rarely'.
test_contract.inference_method: analysis.py downloads the FishBase 24.07 species, country and countref CSVs, keeps species flagged fresh-water only (Fresh, not Brack, not Saltwater) whose AnaCat is not anadromous/catadromous/amphidromous/oceanodromous (16,213 species, 16,174 with native country records), joins their native/endemic country records to FishBase's Continent field, collapses Europe+Asia into Eurasia, and counts species with native records on both sides of each ocean-separated landmass pair. A species is 'robust' if it has >= 2 native countries on each side. Two post-hoc checks, labelled as such in measured.extra.post_hoc, were added after inspecting the output: removing Indonesia/Timor-Leste from the Asian side of the Eurasia|Oceania pair (Indonesian Papua is on New Guinea), and re-running the Eurasia|North America pair with brackish-tolerant non-diadromous species admitted.

claims.label: Water birds disperse seeds and eggs, explaining wide ranges of fresh-water life
claims.statement: The wide distribution of fresh-water plants and lower fresh-water animals depends mainly on the transport of their seeds and eggs by animals, especially wide-flying fresh-water birds that move between often distant bodies of water.
claims.quote: But the wide distribution of fresh-water plants and of the lower animals, whether retaining the same identical form or in some degree modified, I believe mainly depends on the wide dispersal of their seeds and eggs by animals, more especially by fresh-water birds, which have large powers of flight, and naturally travel from one to another and often distant piece of water.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

claims.label: Oceanic islands have fewer species than equal continental areas
claims.statement: Oceanic islands are inhabited by far fewer species of all kinds than continental areas of equal size, a difference not explained by physical conditions.
claims.quote: The species of all kinds which inhabit oceanic islands are few in number compared with those on equal continental areas
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued
claims.notation: I(P - S) = E S \iff S^* = \frac{P I}{I + E};\quad E > 0 \Rightarrow S^* < P;\ \partial S^*/\partial I > 0,\ \partial S^*/\partial E < 0;\quad d_1 < d_2 \Rightarrow S^*(I(d_2)) < S^*(I(d_1))

test_contract.expected_observation: Fit log10(native vascular plant species) = a + b*log10(area km2) + c*|centroid latitude| by ordinary least squares on continental (mainland-connected) TDWG level-3 botanical countries from the World Checklist of Vascular Plants, then predict richness for each pre-registered oceanic island unit at its own area and latitude. Supports if (i) the median ratio of observed to predicted richness across oceanic units is <= 0.5, (ii) >= 80 % of oceanic units lie below the continental prediction, and (iii) a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of the oceanic log-residuals against zero gives p < 0.01.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Refutes if the median observed/predicted ratio is >= 1.0 or fewer than 60 % of oceanic units lie below the prediction. Any other outcome is mixed. Oceanic units whose area lies outside the range of continental areas used in the fit are excluded from the test and listed.
test_contract.inference_method: analysis.py computes the spherical area and area-weighted centroid latitude of each of the 369 TDWG level-3 units and marks a unit 'continental' if any boundary point lies within 2 km of another unit's boundary (241 units after excluding Antarctica), 'oceanic' if in the pre-registered list, and 'other island' otherwise. Native richness per unit is the number of accepted WCVP species with a distribution record flagged neither introduced, extinct nor doubtful. An OLS fit log10 S = a + b log10 A + c |lat| on continental units (b = 0.199, c = -0.0088, R2 = 0.33) predicts richness for each oceanic unit; 28 of 60 oceanic units fall inside the continental area range (196 to 3.84 million km2) and enter the test. The measured value is the median observed/predicted ratio; the rule also requires the fraction below prediction and a one-sided Wilcoxon test.

claims.label: Oceanic islands have a very high proportion of endemic species
claims.statement: Although oceanic islands have few species, the proportion of their species that are endemic (found nowhere else) is often extremely large relative to their area, as expected if occasional colonists arriving in a new isolated district are especially liable to modification.
claims.quote: Although in oceanic islands the number of kinds of inhabitants is scanty, the proportion of endemic species (_i.e._ those found nowhere else in the world) is often extremely large.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued
claims.notation: \sigma(1 - \pi) = m \pi \iff \pi^* = \frac{\sigma}{\sigma + m};\quad m_1 < m_2 \Rightarrow \pi^*(m_2) < \pi^*(m_1);\quad d_1 < d_2 \Rightarrow \pi^*(m(d_1)) < \pi^*(m(d_2))

test_contract.expected_observation: Pre-registered. Using the World Checklist of Vascular Plants, for every TDWG level-3 area compute the native accepted species count S and the proportion E/S of those species that are native to no other level-3 area. Oceanic islands are the 63 level-3 areas pre-registered as 'oceanic' in derived/island_classes.csv; the mainland comparison set is every level-3 area not listed in that file as any kind of island. Areas (km2) are computed from the TDWG WGSRPD level-3 polygons. The claim is SUPPORTED if (i) the median S of oceanic islands is below the median S of mainland areas ('scanty'), (ii) the median E/S of oceanic islands with at least 20 native species is at least twice the median E/S of mainland areas, and (iii) at least 70% of oceanic islands with at least 20 native species lie above the mainland regression line of logit(E/S) on log10(area) ('extremely large relative to their area'). Islands with fewer than 20 native species are excluded from (ii) and (iii) because a proportion is unstable for them.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Pre-registered. The claim is REFUTED if the median E/S of oceanic islands is not greater than the mainland median, or if fewer than 50% of oceanic islands lie above the mainland area regression line. Other outcomes are 'mixed'. Supplementary: the fraction of oceanic islands with E/S >= 0.25, and the same statistics for the 'other-island' class (continental and arc islands), are reported.
test_contract.inference_method: Native (non-introduced, non-doubtful) occurrences of 358,113 accepted non-hybrid WCVP v16 species were tabulated by TDWG level-3 area; a species native to exactly one area was counted as endemic to it. Areas (km2) were computed from the WGSRPD level-3 GeoJSON by spherical polygon area. Islands were classified in advance (derived/island_classes.csv): 63 oceanic, 61 other islands, the rest mainland (Antarctica excluded). Medians of native richness and endemic proportion were compared between the 60 oceanic islands with >= 20 native species and 247 mainland areas; logit(endemic proportion) was regressed on log10(area) for mainland areas and the fraction of oceanic islands above that line computed; a one-sided Mann-Whitney test compared the distributions.

claims.label: Island endemism is low in groups that arrive easily and in numbers
claims.statement: Within one island, some groups are almost wholly endemic while others are not, because groups that immigrate readily and in a body (e.g. marine birds, sea-shells, regularly visiting land-birds) keep their mutual relations undisturbed and so are little modified.
claims.quote: But it by no means follows, that, because in an island nearly all the species of one class are peculiar, those of another class, or of another section of the same class, are peculiar; and this difference seems to depend on the species which do not become modified having immigrated with facility and in a body, so that their mutual relations have not been much disturbed.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

claims.label: Natural selection turns island herbaceous plants into shrubs and trees
claims.statement: Because trees rarely reach distant oceanic islands, herbaceous plants that colonise them gain an advantage by growing taller, so natural selection often converts insular herbaceous plants first into bushes and then into trees, explaining why islands have trees in orders that are elsewhere herbaceous.
claims.quote: If so, natural selection would often tend to add to the stature of herbaceous plants when growing on an island, to whatever order they belonged, and thus convert them first into bushes and ultimately into trees.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

claims.label: Frogs, toads and newts are absent from oceanic islands
claims.statement: Batrachians (frogs, toads and newts) are naturally absent from oceanic islands, not because conditions there are unsuitable (introduced frogs thrive) but because they and their spawn are killed by sea-water and so cannot cross the sea.
claims.quote: Bory St. Vincent long ago remarked that Batrachians (frogs, toads, newts) have never been found on any of the many islands with which the great oceans are studded. I have taken pains to verify this assertion, and I have found it strictly true.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

test_contract.expected_observation: Across a pre-registered list of 40 oceanic island units (see planned unit list in interpretation), zero units have an amphibian species that is endemic to the unit by GBIF occurrence data, where 'endemic' means the species has >= 10 non-fossil, non-captive occurrence records worldwide and >= 95 % of them fall inside the unit. An endemic species cannot be a human introduction, so endemism is used as a conservative proof of native status.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Two or more independent oceanic island units each have at least one endemic amphibian species by the rule above: the universal statement is refuted. Exactly one such unit: 'mixed' (a single counterexample Darwin himself might have disputed, like his New Zealand frog). The proportion of units with native amphibians is reported in either case to characterise the 'general absence' Darwin also asserted.
test_contract.inference_method: analysis.py queries the GBIF occurrence API for class Amphibia (classKey 131) within each of 41 pre-registered oceanic island units (ISO territory code or WGS84 bounding box), excluding fossil and living/captive specimens, and facets by speciesKey. For each species recorded in a unit it fetches the species' global record count (for bounding-box units both counts are restricted to georeferenced records without geospatial issues, so that un-georeferenced museum specimens do not deflate the fraction) and flags the species endemic to the unit if it has >= 10 records worldwide and >= 95 % of them inside the unit. The measured value is the number of units with at least one endemic amphibian; the verdict follows the pre-registered rule (0 supports, 1 mixed, >= 2 refutes).

claims.label: No native terrestrial mammals on islands more than 300 miles from a continent
claims.statement: No native terrestrial mammal inhabits any island more than about 300 miles from a continent or large continental island, even though small mammals thrive when introduced there, because terrestrial mammals cannot cross wide stretches of sea.
claims.quote: as yet I have not found a single instance, free from doubt, of a terrestrial mammal (excluding domesticated animals kept by the natives) inhabiting an island situated above 300 miles from a continent or great continental island;
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

test_contract.expected_observation: Among pre-registered island units whose representative point lies > 482.8 km from the nearest landmass of area >= 100,000 km2 (continents and great islands, computed from Natural Earth 1:50m land polygons), zero units have a non-volant, non-marine mammal species endemic to the unit by GBIF occurrence data (>= 10 non-fossil, non-captive records worldwide, >= 95 % inside the unit). Endemism is used as conservative proof of native status; bats (Chiroptera), cetaceans, sirenians, pinnipeds and Homo sapiens are excluded.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: At least one far unit has >= 2 endemic non-volant terrestrial mammal species, or >= 2 far units each have >= 1: refutes (more than 'a single instance' and not attributable to one doubtful record). Exactly one far unit with exactly one endemic species: mixed. The share of far units with native terrestrial mammals is reported either way.
test_contract.inference_method: analysis.py downloads Natural Earth 1:50m land polygons, computes spherical areas, keeps the 23 landmasses >= 100,000 km2, and measures the great-circle distance from each pre-registered unit's representative point(s) to the nearest densified vertex of those landmasses (excluding a polygon containing the point). 43 of the 52 units lie beyond 482.8 km. For each far unit it facets GBIF Mammalia occurrences by species (country code or bounding box; fossil and living specimens excluded), drops Chiroptera, Cetacea, Sirenia, pinniped and cetacean families and Hominidae via the species API, and flags a species endemic if it has >= 10 records worldwide and >= 95 % inside the unit (for box units both counts are restricted to georeferenced records without geospatial issues, a correction made after the first run showed un-georeferenced museum specimens deflating the fraction). Verdict follows the pre-registered rule.

claims.label: Bats occur on almost every island, often as endemic species
claims.statement: Although terrestrial mammals are absent from oceanic islands, bats occur on almost every island, and remote islands often have their own endemic bat species, because bats can fly across wide spaces of sea and are then modified in their new homes.
claims.quote: Though terrestrial mammals do not occur on oceanic islands, ærial mammals do occur on almost every island.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

test_contract.expected_observation: Using the 43 pre-registered island units lying > 300 statute miles from any landmass >= 100,000 km2 (the far units of darwin1859-ch12-09, same GBIF filters and representative points), a unit counts as 'surveyed' if GBIF holds >= 500 non-fossil, non-captive bird (class Aves) records for it. A surveyed unit 'has bats' if at least one Chiroptera species has >= 5 non-fossil, non-captive GBIF records inside the unit (single records are treated as possible vagrants). A bat species is 'endemic' to a unit if it has >= 10 records worldwide and >= 95 % of them inside the unit (same rule as ch12-09). Supports if >= 80 % of surveyed far units have bats AND >= 33 % of the surveyed far units with bats have >= 1 endemic bat species.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Refutes if < 50 % of surveyed far units have bats, or if < 10 % of the bat-occupied surveyed units have an endemic bat species. Otherwise mixed. The contrast with non-volant mammals is reported descriptively: the number of far units with an endemic bat species is compared with the number having an endemic non-volant terrestrial mammal from the same GBIF endemism rule (1 of 43 in darwin1859-ch12-09).
test_contract.inference_method: analysis.py reads the 43 far island units (> 482.8 km from any landmass >= 100,000 km2) and their GBIF filters from ../darwin1859-ch12-09/derived/units.json. For each unit it counts GBIF bird records (survey proxy, threshold 500), then facets Chiroptera records by speciesKey; for each bat species it fetches the global record count (georeferenced-only for bounding-box units, all records for country-code units) and flags endemism at >= 10 records and >= 95 % inside the unit. A surveyed unit has bats if any species has >= 5 records in it. The pre-registered rule compares the occupancy fraction (thresholds 0.80 / 0.50) and the fraction of bat-occupied units with an endemic bat (0.33 / 0.10). Sensitivities: any single record counts as presence; endemism at >= 80 %.

claims.label: Sea depth between island and mainland predicts their mammalian affinity
claims.statement: Somewhat independently of distance, the depth of sea separating an island from the neighbouring mainland is related to whether they share the same or allied mammal species: islands separated by shallow channels have the same or very similar mammals, those across deep water have distinct species and genera.
claims.quote: there is also a relation, to a certain extent independent of distance, between the depth of the sea separating an island from the neighbouring mainland, and the presence in both of the same mammiferous species or of allied species in a more or less modified condition.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

test_contract.expected_observation: Pre-registered: for each of 28 fixed islands, (i) the terrestrial mammal species set (GBIF Mammalia occurrences with >= 3 records inside the island box, minus bats, cetaceans, sirenians, pinnipeds and 12 domestic or commensal genera), (ii) the same for a fixed neighbouring-mainland box, (iii) channel depth = greatest water depth (GEBCO 2020 via the OpenTopoData API, 100 points) along a fixed straight transect between the nearest island and mainland shores, and (iv) channel width = transect length. f = |island ∩ mainland| / |island|. SUPPORTS if all of: Spearman rho(f, log depth) < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; partial Spearman of f on log depth controlling log width < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; mean f of islands with depth <= 120 m exceeds mean f of islands with depth > 120 m.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Pre-registered: REFUTES if Spearman rho(f, log depth) >= 0 or if mean f of shallow (<= 120 m) islands is <= mean f of deep (> 120 m) islands. Any other outcome is MIXED. Islands with fewer than 5 qualifying species are dropped; with fewer than 12 islands remaining the result is inconclusive (underpowered). If the bathymetry API is unreachable the result is inconclusive (data-unavailable).
test_contract.inference_method: For each of 28 islands the GBIF occurrence API returned speciesKey and genusKey facet counts for Mammalia in the island box and in the mainland box, and the same for Chiroptera, Cetacea, Sirenia, Phocidae, Otariidae, Odobenidae and 12 domestic or commensal genera, which were subtracted; species with >= 3 records formed the sets. f = fraction of island species also present in the mainland set. Channel depth = greatest depth among 100 GEBCO 2020 points along the pre-registered straight transect (OpenTopoData API); width = transect length. Three islands with < 5 qualifying species (Pemba, Lombok, Cyprus) were dropped (n = 25). Spearman's rho between f and log depth, the partial Spearman correlation controlling log width, and the shallow (<= 120 m) vs deep (> 120 m) means were compared with the pre-registered thresholds.

claims.label: Island endemics are related to species of the nearest continent
claims.statement: It is an almost universal rule that the endemic species of islands are related to those of the nearest continent or other nearby islands, even when the islands' physical conditions resemble those of a different, more distant region (e.g. Galapagos to America, Cape Verde to Africa).
claims.quote: indeed it is an almost universal rule that the endemic productions of islands are related to those of the nearest continent, or of other near islands.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

test_contract.expected_observation: In a large majority of island endemics, the nearest relatives outside the island group are native to the nearest continent or the island group's own region.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Nearest outside relatives of island endemics are mostly native to more distant regions.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: An expert checklist coding native ranges on a fixed regional scheme and a phylogeny estimated independently of Darwin's argument; open access; island groups with at least 10 scorable endemics.
test_contract.inference_method: Per endemic, majority rule on native regions of the outside relatives in the smallest clade on the Open Tree genus subtree; share near-related per island group compared with fixed thresholds (pooled >= 0.75 and >= 0.6 in 75% of groups for support; pooled < 0.5 or majority of groups < 0.5 for refutation).

claims.label: Species on islands of one archipelago are closest relatives of each other
claims.statement: The distinct species inhabiting the separate islands of an archipelago are far more closely related to one another than to the inhabitants of any other part of the world, because the islands received immigrants from the same source or from each other.
claims.quote: so that the inhabitants of each separate island, though mostly distinct, are related in an incomparably closer degree to each other than to the inhabitants of any other part of the world.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

test_contract.expected_observation: Most archipelago endemics have as nearest phylogenetic relative another native of the same archipelago, well above a random-relabelling null.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Nearest relatives of archipelago endemics lie outside the archipelago at least as often as inside, or no more often inside than random labelling predicts.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: An expert checklist coding native ranges on a fixed regional scheme, and a phylogeny estimated independently of Darwin's argument covering the relevant genera; open access.
test_contract.inference_method: Nearest-clade composition for each endemic on the genus subtree of the Open Tree synthetic tree; f_in = inside/(inside+outside) compared with a hypergeometric clade-relabelling null simulated per archipelago; thresholds f_in >= 0.67 pooled and p < 0.05 in >= 75% of archipelagos.

claims.label: Naturalised species are usually not closely allied to the natives they join
claims.statement: Species that become naturalised in new countries are generally not closely allied to the native inhabitants but are very distinct, often belonging to genera absent from the region, whereas closely allied species equally well fitted to their places tend to keep separate.
claims.quote: the forms which become naturalised in new countries are not generally closely allied to the aboriginal inhabitants, but are very distinct species, belonging in a large proportion of cases, as shown by Alph. de Candolle, to distinct genera.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

test_contract.expected_observation: Species naturalised in a region are more often in genera absent from its native flora than proven colonists that did not naturalise there.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Naturalised species are as likely or significantly more likely than the colonist pool to belong to genera already native to the region.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: A global, expert-curated vascular plant checklist that codes native versus introduced status per region on a fixed geographic scheme, compiled independently of Darwin and de Candolle; open licence; regions with at least 50 naturalised species.
test_contract.inference_method: Per region, Fisher exact test of genus novelty (genus without native species in the region) for naturalised species versus the pool of species naturalised elsewhere but absent from the region; verdict from the share of regions significant (p < 0.05) in each direction, two-thirds threshold.

claims.label: Inhabitants of any area are modified colonists from the most accessible source
claims.statement: The inhabitants of any area (oceanic islands, mountains, lakes, marshes, caves), where not identical, are plainly related to those of the region from which colonists could most readily have come, the colonists having since been modified and better fitted to their new homes.
claims.quote: The principle which determines the general character of the fauna and flora of oceanic islands, namely, that the inhabitants, when not identically the same, yet are plainly related to the inhabitants of that region whence colonists could most readily have been derived,—the colonists having been subsequently modified and better fitted to their new homes,—is of the widest application throughout nature.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

claims.label: Regions sharing many allied species will also share some identical species
claims.statement: Wherever two regions, however distant, contain many closely allied or representative species, they will also contain some identical species and many doubtful forms ranked variously as species or varieties, showing past migration between them.
claims.quote: And it will, I believe, be universally found to be true, that wherever in two regions, let them be ever so distant, many closely allied or representative species occur, there will likewise be found some identical species
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

claims.label: The lower a group of organisms, the more widely it tends to range
claims.statement: Organisms lower in the scale of nature tend to range more widely than higher ones, because they change more slowly and their seeds and eggs are minute and suited to distant transport.
claims.quote: namely, that the lower any group of organisms is, the more widely it is apt to range.
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

claims.label: Closer relatives tend to be closer together in time and space
claims.statement: Because forms within each class are connected by ordinary generation, the more closely two forms are related by descent, the nearer they will generally be to each other in time and in geographic space.
claims.quote: and the more nearly any two forms are related in blood, the nearer they will generally stand to each other in time and space;
claims.chapter: Ch. XII: Geographical Distribution, continued

test_contract.expected_observation: Space (all extant birds with a range centroid in AVONET and a tip in the BirdTree Hackett MCC tree supplied with AVONET): (S1) the Spearman correlation between patristic distance and great-circle centroid distance across a fixed random sample of 2,000,000 species pairs is positive, and exceeds all of 99 permutations in which centroids are shuffled among species (p <= 0.01); (S2) median centroid distance is strictly ordered congeneric pairs < confamilial non-congeneric pairs < same-order different-family pairs. Time (Paleobiology Database genera of Mammalia and of Mollusca with first-appearance ages and family/order assignments): (T1) in each of the two groups, the median absolute difference in first-appearance midpoint age between pairs of genera in the same family is smaller than between pairs of genera in different families of the same order, and this difference exceeds all of 99 permutations of family labels within orders (p <= 0.01). The space clause passes if S1 and S2 hold; the time clause passes if T1 holds in both groups. Verdict 'supports' if both clauses pass, 'mixed' if one passes, 'refutes' if neither.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: The space clause fails if the Spearman correlation is <= 0 or does not exceed the permutation distribution at p <= 0.01, or if the median distances are not strictly ordered by relatedness. The time clause fails if in either group same-family genus pairs are not closer in first-appearance time than different-family same-order pairs, or the difference is not significant at p <= 0.01 against the within-order permutation null. Both failing refutes the claim.
test_contract.inference_method: Space: 5883 bird species with a one-to-one BirdLife-BirdTree name match, a tree tip and an AVONET range centroid. Patristic distances were computed on the MCC tree; 1999655 random species pairs were drawn and the Spearman correlation between patristic and great-circle centroid distance was compared with 99 permutations of centroids among species; medians of centroid distance were tabulated for congeneric, confamilial and same-order pairs. Time: PBDB accepted genera with family, order and first-appearance ages; within each order, genus pairs (all pairs, or 500000 random pairs for very large orders) were split into same-family and different-family, and the difference of medians of |dFAD| was compared with 99 permutations of family labels within orders.

claims.label: Descent with divergence and extinction produces groups subordinate to groups
claims.statement: The nested arrangement of organisms into groups within groups (species within genera, genera within families, and so on) results from the modified descendants of a single progenitor diverging in character while less divergent forms are exterminated.
claims.quote: he will see that the inevitable result is that the modified descendants proceeding from one progenitor become broken up into groups subordinate to groups.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs
claims.notation: \text{TreeLike}:\ u \le w \wedge v \le w \Rightarrow u \le v \vee v \le u;\quad C(v) = \{w : v \le w\};\quad \text{TreeLike} \iff \forall u v,\ C(u) \cap C(v) = \varnothing \vee C(u) \subseteq C(v) \vee C(v) \subseteq C(u)

claims.label: The Natural System expresses propinquity of descent
claims.statement: The 'something more' than mere resemblance that naturalists seek in the Natural System is closeness of descent, which is the only known cause of similarity among organisms and is partially revealed by classifications.
claims.quote: propinquity of descent,—the only known cause of the similarity of organic beings,—is the bond, hidden as it is by various degrees of modification, which is partially revealed to us by our classifications.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Characters least modified by adaptation are most constant and useful in classification
claims.statement: The value of a character for classification depends on its constancy across large groups of species, and characters are constant when they have been little changed in adapting species to their conditions of life; hence parts least concerned with special habits are generally the most useful for classification.
claims.quote: But their importance for classification, I believe, depends on their greater constancy throughout large groups of species; and this constancy depends on such organs having generally been subjected to less change in the adaptation of the species to their conditions of life.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Higher taxonomic ranks are almost arbitrary
claims.statement: The relative value of groups such as orders, sub-orders, families, sub-families and genera is, at least at present, almost arbitrary, as shown by groups being raised in rank merely because more allied species were discovered.
claims.quote: Finally, with respect to the comparative value of the various groups of species, such as orders, sub-orders, families, sub-families, and genera, they seem to be, at least at present, almost arbitrary.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Branches equally related by descent can differ greatly in amount of modification
claims.statement: A natural arrangement of groups must be strictly genealogical, but branches that are equally closely related to a common progenitor may differ greatly in how much they have been modified, and these differing amounts of difference are what is expressed by ranking them as different genera, families or orders.
claims.quote: I believe that the _arrangement_ of the groups within each class, in due subordination and relation to the other groups, must be strictly genealogical in order to be natural; but that the _amount_ of difference in the several branches or groups, though allied in the same degree in blood to their common progenitor, may differ greatly, being due to the different degrees of modification which they have undergone
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Varieties form nested groups for the same reason species do
claims.statement: Domestic and natural varieties fall into groups subordinate to groups (sub-varieties under varieties under species) for the same reason species do, namely closeness of descent combined with various degrees of modification.
claims.quote: The origin of the existence of groups subordinate to groups, is the same with varieties as with species, namely, closeness of descent with various degrees of modification.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs
claims.notation: \text{TreeLike}(\alpha) \Rightarrow \forall u v,\ C(u) \cap C(v) = \varnothing \vee C(u) \subseteq C(v) \vee C(v) \subseteq C(u),\ \text{for any type } \alpha \text{ of forms}

claims.label: Characters shared across species with very different habits indicate common inheritance
claims.statement: However trifling a character, if it occurs throughout many species with very different habits of life it can be explained only by inheritance from a common parent, and so has high value for classification; for the same reason rudimentary structures can be as useful as other parts.
claims.quote: if it prevail throughout many and different species, especially those having very different habits of life, it assumes high value; for we can account for its presence in so many forms with such different habits, only by its inheritance from a common parent.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Distinct lineages adapted to similar conditions converge in external form
claims.statement: Animals from very distinct lines of descent can become adapted to similar conditions and so acquire a close external resemblance; such analogical or adaptive resemblances conceal rather than reveal blood-relationship, so they are almost worthless for classification between groups, although the same characters can indicate true affinity within a group.
claims.quote: For animals, belonging to two most distinct lines of descent, may readily become adapted to similar conditions, and thus assume a close external resemblance; but such resemblances will not reveal—will rather tend to conceal their blood-relationship to their proper lines of descent.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

test_contract.expected_observation: Using AVONET (Tobias et al. 2022) species-level external measurements (beak length culmen, beak length nares, beak width, beak depth, tarsus length, wing length, Kipp's distance, secondary1, hand-wing index, tail length, body mass; log-transformed and z-scored) and AVONET ecological categories (trophic niche, primary lifestyle, habitat), three clauses are tested. (a) Convergence: among all between-order species pairs, the mean standardized Euclidean morphological distance of pairs with identical niche (same trophic niche AND same primary lifestyle) is at least 10% smaller than that of pairs with different trophic niche AND different primary lifestyle, with a permutation p < 0.01 (niche labels shuffled among species, 200 permutations). (b) Concealment between groups: leave-one-out k-nearest-neighbour (k = 5) prediction from morphology yields a Cohen's kappa for ecological niche (trophic niche x primary lifestyle combination) that is higher than the kappa for taxonomic order. (c) Affinity within groups: among orders with >= 3 families and >= 30 species, leave-one-out k-NN prediction of family from morphology (congeners excluded from the neighbour pool) gives kappa > 0.3 in a majority of such orders. Verdict 'supports' if all three clauses pass; 'mixed' if one or two pass; 'refutes' if none passes.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Clause (a) fails if same-niche between-order pairs are not at least 10% closer in morphology than different-niche pairs, or the permutation p >= 0.01. Clause (b) fails if morphology predicts order with kappa >= that for niche. Clause (c) fails if kappa for family within order is <= 0.3 in half or more of the eligible orders. No clause passing refutes the claim; (a) failing alone already refutes the central convergence statement and is reported as 'mixed' only if (b) or (c) pass.
test_contract.inference_method: AVONET1 (BirdLife taxonomy) species with complete values for 11 external measurements were log-transformed and z-scored (n = 10999). (a) For every between-order species pair the Euclidean distance was computed; the mean distance for pairs with identical trophic niche and primary lifestyle was compared with pairs differing in both, and the ratio was tested against 200 permutations of niche labels across species. (b) Leave-one-out 5-nearest-neighbour prediction from morphology was scored with Cohen's kappa for niche (trophic niche x lifestyle) and for order. (c) Within each order with >= 3 families and >= 30 species, family was predicted by LOO 5-NN with congeners excluded from the neighbour pool, and kappa recorded.

claims.label: Expanding dominant groups explain why all life falls into a few great classes
claims.statement: Larger and more dominant groups tend to keep increasing in size and to supplant smaller, feebler groups, which is why all organisms, recent and extinct, fall into a few great orders, still fewer classes, and a single natural system.
claims.quote: The larger and more dominant groups thus tend to go on increasing in size; and they consequently supplant many smaller and feebler groups. Thus we can account for the fact that all organisms, recent and extinct, are included under a few great orders, under still fewer classes, and all in one great natural system.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Aberrant groups are species-poor relicts of extinction
claims.statement: Aberrant or osculant groups are the surviving remnants of failing groups that suffered heavy extinction; consequently they are generally represented by very few species, and those species are usually very distinct from each other.
claims.quote: And we have some evidence of aberrant forms having suffered severely from extinction, for they are generally represented by extremely few species; and such species as do occur are generally very distinct from each other, which again implies extinction.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Affinities of one group to another are usually general, not to any single species
claims.statement: When a member of one group shows a real affinity to a quite distinct group, the affinity is usually general rather than to any particular species, because it retains characters of an ancient common progenitor of both groups.
claims.quote: when a member belonging to one group of animals exhibits an affinity to a quite distinct group, this affinity in most cases is general and not special
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Gaps between groups, even whole classes, are due to extinction of connecting forms
claims.statement: Extinction has defined and widened the intervals between groups; even the distinctness of whole classes, such as birds from other vertebrates, results from the loss of many ancient forms that once connected their early progenitors.
claims.quote: We may thus account even for the distinctness of whole classes from each other—for instance, of birds from all other vertebrate animals—by the belief that many ancient forms of life have been utterly lost, through which the early progenitors of birds were formerly connected with the early progenitors of the other vertebrate classes.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Homologous parts change shape and size but keep the same relative connexions
claims.statement: Within a class, homologous parts may change to almost any extent in form and size but always remain connected in the same order; for example, the bones of the arm and forearm are never transposed.
claims.quote: the parts may change to almost any extent in form and size, and yet they always remain connected together in the same order.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Unity of type reflects a common progenitor's pattern modified by slight steps
claims.statement: The shared pattern of homologous organs within a class is explained by descent from an ancient progenitor (an archetype) that already had that pattern, which natural selection then modified by slight successive steps for different uses without transposing parts.
claims.quote: If we suppose that the ancient progenitor, the archetype as it may be called, of all mammals, had its limbs constructed on the existing general pattern, for whatever purpose they served, we can at once perceive the plain signification of the homologous construction of the limbs throughout the whole class.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Serially homologous parts derive from many repeated similar elements in progenitors
claims.statement: Serial homologies within one individual (skull and vertebrae, jaws and legs of crustaceans, floral parts and leaves) arise because the progenitors of vertebrates, articulates and flowering plants had many repeated similar parts, which natural selection adapted to diverse purposes while inheritance retained a fundamental resemblance.
claims.quote: An indefinite repetition of the same part or organ is the common characteristic (as Owen has observed) of all low or little-modified forms; therefore we may readily believe that the unknown progenitor of the vertebrata possessed many vertebræ; the unknown progenitor of the articulata, many segments; and the unknown progenitor of flowering plants, many spiral whorls of leaves.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Embryos of different animals in the same class are strikingly similar
claims.statement: Embryos of distinct animals within the same class are often strikingly similar, more so than the adults, and the points of resemblance often have no direct relation to their conditions of existence.
claims.quote: The embryos, also, of distinct animals within the same class are often strikingly similar
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Active larvae are adapted to their own conditions as fully as adults
claims.statement: Whenever an embryo or larva becomes active and must provide for itself, it is as perfectly adapted to its conditions of life as the adult, and such adaptations can make the larvae of allied species differ as much as or more than their adults, though most larvae still follow the law of embryonic resemblance.
claims.quote: The period of activity may come on earlier or later in life; but whenever it comes on, the adaptation of the larva to its conditions of life is just as perfect and as beautiful as in the adult animal.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Young of domestic breeds differ much less than adults
claims.statement: The characteristic differences between domestic breeds produced by man's selection (in dogs, horses and pigeons) generally do not appear early in life and are inherited at a corresponding later age, so that the young of different breeds differ far less in proportions than the adults, with occasional exceptions such as the short-faced tumbler pigeon.
claims.quote: the characteristic differences which give value to each breed, and which have been accumulated by man’s selection, have not generally first appeared at an early period of life, and have been inherited by the offspring at a corresponding not early period.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Community of embryonic structure reveals community of descent
claims.statement: Because the embryo is the animal in a less modified state that partly reveals the structure of its progenitor, two groups that pass through the same or similar embryonic stages are descended from the same or similar parents, however different their adults; this is why embryonic characters are the most valuable for classification.
claims.quote: Thus, community in embryonic structure reveals community of descent.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Ancient extinct forms should resemble the embryos of their living descendants
claims.statement: Since embryos partly show the structure of less modified ancient progenitors, ancient and extinct forms should resemble the embryos of their living descendants, though this may be obscured by early-appearing variations and may be undemonstrable because the geological record does not reach back far enough.
claims.quote: we can clearly see why ancient and extinct forms of life should resemble the embryos of their descendants,—our existing species.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Embryological facts follow from late-appearing variations inherited at corresponding ages
claims.statement: The leading facts of embryology are explained because, in the descendants of a common progenitor, successive slight modifications generally do not appear at a very early period of life (though they may be caused earlier) and are inherited at a corresponding later age, leaving embryos little modified.
claims.quote: the leading facts in embryology, which are second in importance to none in natural history, are explained on the principle of slight modifications not appearing, in the many descendants from some one ancient progenitor, at a very early period in the life of each, though perhaps caused at the earliest, and being inherited at a corresponding not early period.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Rudimentary organs are extremely common throughout nature
claims.statement: Rudimentary, atrophied or aborted organs that bear the stamp of uselessness are extremely common in animals and plants.
claims.quote: Organs or parts in this strange condition, bearing the stamp of inutility, are extremely common throughout nature.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Rudimentary organs are highly variable
claims.statement: Rudimentary organs vary greatly in development among individuals of the same species, and the degree of reduction of the same organ can differ much between closely allied species; because they are useless, their variations are not checked by natural selection.
claims.quote: Rudimentary organs in the individuals of the same species are very liable to vary in degree of development and in other respects.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Rudimentary organs are relatively larger in the embryo than in the adult
claims.statement: As a universal rule, a rudimentary part is relatively larger compared with adjoining parts in the embryo than in the adult, and some rudiments (such as the teeth of whales and ruminants) appear in the embryo and then wholly disappear.
claims.quote: It is also, I believe, a universal rule, that a rudimentary part or organ is of greater size relatively to the adjoining parts in the embryo, than in the adult
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Disuse is the main cause of rudimentary organs
claims.statement: Disuse over successive generations has been the main agency reducing organs to rudiments (as with eyes of cave animals and wings of island birds), aided by natural selection where an organ becomes injurious; because reduction occurs at maturity and is inherited at a corresponding age, rudiments remain relatively larger in the embryo.
claims.quote: I believe that disuse has been the main agency; that it has led in successive generations to the gradual reduction of various organs, until they have become rudimentary
claims.chapter: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

claims.label: Descent with modification embraces all members of each class
claims.statement: Because all members of whole classes are linked by chains of affinities, fossils fill wide gaps between orders, rudiments imply fully developed ancestral organs, and structures within a class share one pattern and similar embryos, descent with modification embraces all members of the same class.
claims.quote: Therefore I cannot doubt that the theory of descent with modification embraces all the members of the same class.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

test_contract.expected_observation: Pre-registered: for 22 classes as circumscribed in the Cuvier/Owen system current in 1859, each represented by 3-7 fixed modern taxa, an induced subtree of the Open Tree of Life synthetic tree is obtained. For each class, membership is coded on the tips and reconstructed by weighted parsimony (gain cost 2, loss cost 1; among equally cheap reconstructions the one with fewest gains); the number of origins = gains + 1 if the root is reconstructed as a member. A class is 'of single descent' if origins = 1. SUPPORTS if at least 80% of the classes (>= 18 of 22) are of single descent.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Pre-registered: REFUTES if 50% or fewer of the classes (<= 11 of 22) are of single descent. Between 12 and 17 is MIXED. If the Open Tree API is unreachable or fewer than 85% of the representative taxa can be placed as tips, the result is inconclusive (data-unavailable). The Dollo count (number of maximal all-member clades) is recorded as a secondary descriptive statistic.
test_contract.inference_method: The 103 pre-registered representative taxa were resolved with the Open Tree TNRS (exact matches, context All life; Pteropoda did not match) and an induced subtree of the synthetic tree was requested. Eleven further taxa are non-monophyletic in the synthesis and mapped to internal nodes already containing other sampled tips, so 91 of 103 (0.88) were placed as tips. For each 1859 class the tips were coded as members or not and the cheapest reconstruction under weighted parsimony (gain 2, loss 1, ties broken toward fewer gains) was found by dynamic programming over the (polytomous) tree; origins = gains, plus one if the root is reconstructed as a member. The Dollo count of maximal all-member clades was recorded alongside.

claims.label: Animals from at most four or five progenitors, plants from as many or fewer
claims.statement: All animals have descended from at most four or five progenitors, and all plants from an equal or smaller number.
claims.quote: I believe that animals have descended from at most only four or five progenitors, and plants from an equal or lesser number.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

test_contract.expected_observation: Pre-registered: on the Open Tree of Life synthetic tree induced on a fixed set of major lineages (listed below with their 1859 kingdom assignment), count for each kingdom the Dollo number of progenitors = number of maximal clades whose tips all belong to that kingdom (tips of the other kingdom or of neither break a clade). Two readings are scored. Modern reading: animals = Metazoa, plants = Embryophyta + the other Archaeplastida. 1859 reading: animals = Metazoa plus the 'Protozoa' then placed among animals (Infusoria, Rhizopoda, Gregarinida), plants = land plants, green, red and brown algae, diatoms, fungi and blue-green algae. SUPPORTS if under BOTH readings animal progenitors <= 5 and plant progenitors <= animal progenitors.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Pre-registered: REFUTES if under the modern reading animal progenitors > 5 or plant progenitors > animal progenitors. MIXED if the modern reading satisfies both conditions but the 1859 reading violates either. If the Open Tree API is unreachable or fewer than 90% of the listed lineages map to the tree, the result is inconclusive (data-unavailable).
test_contract.inference_method: The 25 pre-registered lineage names were resolved with the Open Tree TNRS (exact matches, context All life) and an induced subtree of the synthetic tree was requested. Radiolaria and Charophyta are pruned from the synthesis and Proteobacteria and Firmicutes are non-monophyletic and map to internal nodes, so 21 of 25 lineages (0.84) could be placed as tips, below the pre-registered 0.9 threshold. The Dollo progenitor count (maximal clades whose tips all belong to the kingdom; tips of the other kingdom or of neither break a clade) was nevertheless computed for both readings and is reported as exploratory.

claims.label: All living things share chemical composition, cell structure and laws of growth
claims.statement: All living things have much in common in their chemical composition, germinal vesicles, cellular structure, and laws of growth and reproduction, as shown even by the same poison often affecting plants and animals similarly.
claims.quote: Nevertheless all living things have much in common, in their chemical composition, their germinal vesicles, their cellular structure, and their laws of growth and reproduction.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

test_contract.expected_observation: Pre-registered. Twenty marker families are fixed in advance (KEGG Orthology ids): 15 aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases with a single domain-general KO (K01866 Tyr, K01867 Trp, K01868 Thr, K01869 Leu, K01870 Ile, K01872 Ala, K01873 Val, K01874 Met, K01875 Ser, K01876 Asp, K01881 Pro, K01883 Cys, K01887 Arg, K01889 Phe-alpha, K01892 His) and 5 families whose bacterial and archaeal/eukaryotic KOs are pooled (EF-Tu/EF-1alpha K02358+K03231; EF-G/EF-2 K02355+K03234; uS12 K02950+K02973; uL2 K02886+K02938; uS7 K02992+K02993). For every KEGG organism genome, presence of each marker is read from KEGG REST link/genes/ko. The claim is SUPPORTED if, in each of the three domains (Bacteria, Archaea, Eukaryotes as grouped in KEGG BRITE br08601), at least 95% of genomes carry at least 18 of the 20 markers, and every marker is present in at least 90% of the genomes of every domain.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Pre-registered. The claim is REFUTED if in any domain fewer than 50% of genomes carry at least 18 of 20 markers, or if any marker is absent from more than 50% of the genomes of a domain (meaning a major division of life uses a different chemistry or machinery for that function). Other outcomes are 'mixed'. The distribution of marker counts, the identity of genomes with the fewest markers, and per-marker prevalence by domain are reported.
test_contract.inference_method: All 11,950 KEGG organism genomes (10,148 Bacteria, 469 Archaea, 1,333 Eukaryotes per BRITE br08601) were scored for presence of the 20 pre-registered marker families using KEGG REST link/genes/ko for each KO. 96.9% of genomes carry >= 18 of 20 markers (Bacteria 97.0%, Archaea 96.0%, Eukaryotes 96.3%); 83.8% carry all 20. The pre-registered rule nevertheless returns 'refutes' because the AspRS marker (K01876) is found in only 1.5% of Archaea: KEGG files the archaeal (and many bacterial) non-discriminating aspartyl-tRNA synthetase under a different orthology id, K09759. A post-hoc sensitivity analysis pooling K09759 into AspRS was added and is labelled as such in analysis.py and measured.extra; under it AspRS prevalence in Archaea is 87.4% and the only other marker below the 90% universality threshold is CysRS in Archaea (87.6%), giving 'mixed' under the pre-registered support rule.

claims.label: Probably all organisms descend from one primordial form
claims.statement: By analogy, probably all organisms that have ever lived on earth have descended from a single primordial form.
claims.quote: Therefore I should infer from analogy that probably all the organic beings which have ever lived on this earth have descended from some one primordial form, into which life was first breathed.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

claims.label: Species differ from varieties only in their intermediates having existed formerly
claims.statement: The only distinction between species and well-marked varieties is that varieties are known or believed to be connected by intermediate gradations at present, whereas species were connected by them in the past; species should therefore be treated, like genera, as combinations made for convenience.
claims.quote: Hereafter we shall be compelled to acknowledge that the only distinction between species and well-marked varieties is, that the latter are known, or believed, to be connected at the present day by intermediate gradations, whereas species were formerly thus connected.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

claims.label: Organism-to-organism relations are the most important cause of organic change
claims.statement: The most important cause of organic change is the mutual relation of organism to organism, in which the improvement of one form causes the improvement or extermination of others; this is almost independent of changes, even sudden ones, in physical conditions.
claims.quote: the most important of all causes of organic change is one which is almost independent of altered and perhaps suddenly altered physical conditions, namely, the mutual relation of organism to organism,—the improvement of one being entailing the improvement or the extermination of others
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

claims.label: Amount of fossil change between formations measures elapsed time
claims.statement: Because species are produced and exterminated by slow, still-acting causes, the amount of organic change in the fossils of consecutive formations is probably a fair, though imperfect, measure of the time elapsed, and can be used to estimate the length of the blank intervals between formations.
claims.quote: it follows, that the amount of organic change in the fossils of consecutive formations probably serves as a fair measure of the lapse of actual time.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

test_contract.expected_observation: Using Paleobiology Database stage-level diversity tables for marine animal genera (occs/diversity, count=genera, time_reso=stage, Phanerozoic, marine environments), turnover T_i for each stage i = (X_bL + X_FL) / (X_bt + X_bL + X_Ft + X_FL), the fraction of genera sampled in or ranging through stage i that make their last appearance in it, and duration D_i = early age minus late age of the stage (PBDB/ICS ages). The last two stages (Pleistocene edge, where last appearances are distorted by the Recent) are excluded. Pass if (1) the Spearman correlation between T_i and D_i across stages is positive with p < 0.05, AND (2) the partial Spearman correlation controlling for log(number of occurrences in the stage) is also positive with p < 0.05, AND (3) the correlation remains positive (point estimate > 0) when the five stages with the highest turnover (mass-extinction stages) are removed, so that the relation is not carried by catastrophes alone. 'Fair though imperfect' is operationalised as rho between 0.2 and 0.9: a rho >= 0.2 that meets (1)-(3) supports; the verdict is 'mixed' if (1) holds but (2) or (3) fails, 'refutes' if (1) fails.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Refuted if turnover between consecutive stages does not increase with stage duration (Spearman rho <= 0 or p >= 0.05), which would mean faunal change carries no information about elapsed time. Mixed if the raw correlation is positive but disappears when sampling intensity is controlled or is carried entirely by the five highest-turnover stages.
test_contract.inference_method: The PBDB diversity table for marine animal genera at stage resolution was downloaded for the whole Phanerozoic; for each of the 96 stages retained (two youngest dropped) turnover was computed as the share of genera present that make their last appearance in the stage, and stage duration as the difference of its PBDB/ICS boundary ages. Spearman correlation of turnover with duration, the partial Spearman correlation controlling log occurrences, and the correlation after removing the five highest-turnover stages (Stage 4, Changhsingian, Drumian, Guzhangian, Katian) were computed.

claims.label: Rate of organic change was slower early in life's history
claims.statement: In early periods of earth's history, when forms of life were fewer and simpler, the rate of organic change was probably slower, and at the first dawn of life it may have been extremely slow.
claims.quote: During early periods of the earth’s history, when the forms of life were probably fewer and simpler, the rate of change was probably slower; and at the first dawn of life, when very few forms of the simplest structure existed, the rate of change may have been slow in an extreme degree.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

claims.label: Known geological history is a fragment of the time since the first organism
claims.statement: The whole history of the world as known from geology is only a small fragment of the time that has elapsed since the first organism, the progenitor of all later forms, came into existence.
claims.quote: The whole history of the world, as at present known, although of a length quite incomprehensible by us, will hereafter be recognised as a mere fragment of time, compared with the ages which have elapsed since the first creature, the progenitor of innumerable extinct and living descendants, was created.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

claims.label: Every mental power was acquired by gradation
claims.statement: Each mental power and capacity must have been acquired gradually, so psychology will rest on this foundation, and light will be thrown on the origin of man and his history.
claims.quote: Psychology will be based on a new foundation, that of the necessary acquirement of each mental power and capacity by gradation.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

claims.label: Few living species will leave descendants; common species of dominant groups will prevail
claims.statement: Very few living species will leave descendants in the far future, and those that will prevail and give rise to new dominant species will be the common, widespread species of the larger, dominant groups.
claims.quote: We can so far take a prophetic glance into futurity as to foretel that it will be the common and widely-spread species, belonging to the larger and dominant groups, which will ultimately prevail and procreate new and dominant species.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

claims.label: Succession by generation has never been broken by a world-wide cataclysm
claims.statement: Since all living forms are lineal descendants of forms that lived long before the Silurian epoch, the ordinary succession by generation has never once been broken and no cataclysm has ever desolated the whole world.
claims.quote: As all the living forms of life are the lineal descendants of those which lived long before the Silurian epoch, we may feel certain that the ordinary succession by generation has never once been broken, and that no cataclysm has desolated the whole world.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

test_contract.expected_observation: Using PBDB occs/diversity stage-level tables for marine Animalia genera (Phanerozoic) and the same table for each of nine marine animal phyla/classes (Mollusca, Brachiopoda, Arthropoda, Echinodermata, Cnidaria, Bryozoa, Porifera, Annelida, Chordata), define for each stage i the boundary-crossing fraction C_i = (X_bt + X_Ft) / (X_bt + X_Ft + X_bL + X_FL), the share of genera present in stage i that are also recorded after it (range-through or first-appearing and continuing). Exclude the two youngest stages (Recent edge). Pass if (1) the minimum C_i over all retained Phanerozoic stage boundaries is >= 0.10 (at no point did fewer than one in ten marine genera survive), AND (2) at the stage with the minimum C_i, at least 7 of the 9 phyla/classes have C_i > 0 (survivors in at least seven major lineages), AND (3) the median C_i over all stages is >= 0.5. Verdict 'supports' if all three hold; 'mixed' if (1) and (2) hold but (3) fails, or if (1) fails only marginally (0.05 <= min C_i < 0.10) while (2) holds; 'refutes' if any boundary has min C_i < 0.05 or fewer than 7 of 9 lineages have survivors at the worst boundary.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Refuted if the fossil record contains a stage boundary across which fewer than 5% of marine animal genera persist, or at which survivors are absent from three or more of the nine major lineages, which would indicate a near-total biotic reset incompatible with unbroken descent. The Precambrian part of the claim ('long before the Silurian') cannot be tested with this data and is excluded from the verdict.
test_contract.inference_method: For each of 96 Phanerozoic stages (two youngest dropped) the fraction of marine animal genera present that are also recorded after the stage (X_bt + X_Ft over all present) was computed from the PBDB diversity table. The stage with the lowest crossing fraction (Stage 4) was identified and the same table was retrieved for nine major lineages to count survivors across that boundary.

claims.label: Natural selection makes endowments tend towards perfection
claims.statement: Because natural selection works solely by and for the good of each being, all bodily and mental endowments will tend to progress towards perfection.
claims.quote: And as natural selection works solely by and for the good of each being, all corporeal and mental endowments will tend to progress towards perfection.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

claims.label: The 'entangled bank' laws produce the diversity of living forms
claims.statement: The varied and interdependent forms of life were produced by laws still acting: growth with reproduction; inheritance; variability caused by external conditions and by use and disuse; a rate of increase high enough to cause a struggle for life and so natural selection, which in turn causes divergence of character and extinction of less improved forms.
claims.quote: These laws, taken in the largest sense, being Growth with Reproduction; Inheritance which is almost implied by reproduction; Variability from the indirect and direct action of the external conditions of life, and from use and disuse; a Ratio of Increase so high as to lead to a Struggle for Life, and as a consequence to Natural Selection, entailing Divergence of Character and the Extinction of less-improved forms.
claims.chapter: Ch. XIV: Recapitulation and Conclusion

claims.label: Reliance on chance variation and natural selection stalls inquiry into physical causes
claims.statement: As long as fortuitous variation and the survival of the fittest are accepted as sufficient explanations in biology, they will tend to hold back careful investigation of the real physical causes of organic form.
claims.quote: So long and so far as “fortuitous variation” and the “survival of the fittest” remain engrained as fundamental and satisfactory hypotheses in the philosophy of biology, so long will these “satisfactory and specious causes” tend to stay “severe and diligent inquiry,”
claims.chapter: Ch. I: Introductory

claims.label: Cells, tissues, shells, bones, leaves and flowers are shaped by the laws of physics
claims.statement: The material parts of living things (cells, tissues, shells, bones, leaves, flowers) are portions of matter whose particles have been moved, moulded and shaped in obedience to the laws of physics.
claims.quote: Cell and tissue, shell and bone, leaf and flower, are so many portions of matter, and it is in obedience to the laws of physics that their particles have been moved, moulded and conformed.
claims.chapter: Ch. I: Introductory

claims.label: Problems of organic form are mathematical and problems of growth are physical
claims.statement: The problems of the form of living things are, in the first instance, mathematical problems and their problems of growth are essentially physical problems, so morphology is a branch of physical science.
claims.quote: Their problems of form are in the first instance mathematical problems, and their problems of growth are essentially physical problems; and the morphologist is, _ipso facto_, a student of physical science.
claims.chapter: Ch. I: Introductory

claims.label: No known physical law is transgressed by the bodily mechanism
claims.statement: However complex living processes are, no physical law (including those of chemistry, surface action and osmosis) is known to be broken by the working of the body.
claims.quote: But all the while, so far as I am aware, no physical law, any more than that of gravity itself, not even among the puzzles of chemical “stereometry,” or of physiological “surface-action” or “osmosis,” is known to be _transgressed_ by the bodily mechanism.
claims.chapter: Ch. I: Introductory

claims.label: The form of an object is a diagram of the forces acting or that have acted on it
claims.statement: The form of any portion of matter, living or dead, can be read as a diagram of forces: from the shape of a solid one can deduce the forces that produced and maintain it, and from the shape of a fluid the forces currently acting on it, so an organism's conformation is explained by a balance of forces.
claims.quote: In short, the form of an object is a “diagram of forces,” in this sense, at least, that from it we can judge of or deduce the forces that are acting or have acted upon it
claims.chapter: Ch. I: Introductory

claims.label: Surface tension at a cell's boundary strongly affects its form
claims.statement: Like other fluid bodies, the surface of a cell such as an Amoeba carries a surface tension that depends on the substance it touches, and this surface tension strongly affects the cell's form.
claims.quote: Like other fluid bodies, its surface, whatsoever other substance, gas, liquid or solid, it be in contact with, and in varying degree according to the nature of that adjacent substance, is the seat of molecular force exhibiting itself as a surface-tension, from the action of which many important consequences follow, which greatly affect the form of the fluid surface.
claims.chapter: Ch. I: Introductory

morpholib.note: DITH sets each cell interfacial tension by cortical tension minus adhesion to the specific neighbour, so the tension depends on what the surface touches and drives germ-layer cell shape and sorting, as the claim asserts.
