claims.label: Cell domains make coordinated group decisions, even random ones
claims.statement: Cells join into domains that make decisions as a single unit: when left-right asymmetry is randomized in early embryos, a whole domain picks L or R identity rather than individual cells choosing independently, and in frog melanoma-like conversion all melanocytes in a body convert or not together.
claims.quote: Remarkably, however, this randomization is made on a group level – in each case, the entire domain randomly picks L or R identity, not exhibiting a speckled appearance where each cell adopts a stochastic outcome. The decision is random, but all of the cells in the domain are coordinated to make the same random decision (Levin et al., 2002).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin

claims.label: Neural motor control may be an exaptation of bioelectric navigation of morphospace
claims.statement: Neural control of body movement in three-dimensional space may be an evolutionary exaptation and speed-up of an older, slower role of bioelectric signalling: moving the body's configuration through anatomical morphospace during embryogenesis, repair and remodelling.
claims.quote: Neural networks control the movement of a body in three-dimensional space; this scheme may be an evolutionary exaptation and speed-optimization of a more ancient, slower role of bioelectrical signaling: the movement of body configuration through anatomical morphospace during embryogenesis, repair, and remodeling (Sullivan et al., 2016; Mathews and Levin, 2018; Mclaughlin and Levin, 2018).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin

claims.label: Brain cognition lies on a continuum with conserved pre-neural computation
claims.statement: Given the deep evolutionary conservation of ion-channel and neurotransmitter mechanisms between developmental and behavioural processes, the cognitive capacities of advanced brains are likely on a continuum with, and evolved from, much simpler computational processes conserved at both the functional and molecular levels.
claims.quote: Thus, it is likely that the cognitive capacities of advanced brains lie on a continuum with, and evolve from, much simpler computational processes that are widely conserved at both the functional and mechanism (molecular) levels.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Body Patterning and Cognition: A Common Origin

claims.label: Disrupting or restoring cell communication should trigger or suppress cancer
claims.statement: The shrinking-Self view of cancer predicts that interfering with physiological communication among cells should be able to trigger cancer and restoring it should suppress cancer, and that the relevant parameter (communication) is spread over considerable distance rather than confined to single cells as genomic damage is.
claims.quote: This view predicts that interference with (or restoration of) physiological communication among cells should be able to trigger (or suppress) cancer and that the relevant parameter (communication) is spread out over considerable distance and not confined to single cells (e.g., genomic damage).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self

claims.label: Depolarization induces and hyperpolarization prevents tumour-like changes in tadpoles
claims.statement: In tadpoles, depolarizing a specific cell population is sufficient to cause metastatic-like transformation of normal melanocytes in genetically normal animals, while optogenetic or constitutive hyperpolarization prevents human oncogenes from inducing tumours.
claims.quote: metastatic transformation of normal melanocytes can be achieved in genetically normal tadpoles simply by depolarizing a specific cell population (Lobikin et al., 2012), while, conversely, human oncogenes which normally induce tumors can be prevented from doing so simply by optogenetic or constitutive hyperpolarization (Chernet and Levin, 2013b, 2014; Chernet et al., 2015, 2016).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self

claims.label: Cancer cells are no more selfish than normal cells; their self is smaller
claims.statement: Cells in a metazoan body are not less selfish than unicellular organisms or cancer cells; all are equally selfish, but the self that normal somatic cells defend is larger in space, time and complexity, its boundary being set by how far information passes between subunits.
claims.quote: They are equally selfish, working only for the benefit of themselves, but the relevant self that they defend is bigger in terms of space, time, and complexity. As will be argued below, what defines this Self is the boundary of information being able to pass between the subunits.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self

claims.label: Most biological systems consist of multiple nested selves
claims.statement: Under Scale-Free Cognition, most biological systems consist of multiple, nested selves rather than one, each inner agent maintaining its own Self only to the extent that it restricts information flow from its neighbours.
claims.quote: It is an essential aspect of Scale-Free Cognition that most biological systems consist of multiple, nested selves [not one, as implied by Integrated Information Theory (Tononi, 2008)].
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self

claims.label: An Individual is defined by the scale and types of goals it can pursue
claims.statement: The scale and types of goals (in the cybernetic sense of feedback toward a specific state) that a system can pursue define the boundaries and content of that system as an agent or Individual; the coherent Self is the set of parts that operate together toward specific goal states.
claims.quote: I propose a definition of an Individual based on its information-processing structure (Barandiaran et al., 2009): the scale and types of goals that a system can pursue defines (determines) the boundaries and content of the putative “agent.”
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Defining Individuation From a Cognitive Perspective

claims.label: Cognitive light cones have expanded over evolutionary time
claims.statement: The volume of possible cognitive light cones (spatio-temporal boundaries of agents' goals) has presumably kept expanding over evolutionary time, through innovations in body structure that drastically enlarge the cognitive boundary, although some lineages contract it permanently or in particular life stages.
claims.quote: Presumably, the volume of possible cognitive light cones keeps expanding with evolutionary time (although some lineages can contract it, permanently or during specific ontogenetic life stages). Over evolutionary scales, there have been “inflationary leaps” – innovations in body structure which drastically increase the cognitive boundary of viable selves.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Defining Individuation From a Cognitive Perspective

claims.label: Memory and learning are the origin of developmental modularity
claims.statement: Memory can be the beginning of modularity because learning compresses complex states into simple triggers; in somatic control networks this appears as developmental modules in which a single simple driver (e.g. a bioelectric state) initiates a complex morphogenetic cascade such as building an eye or hand.
claims.quote: Importantly, memory can serve as the beginning of modularity because learning essentially groups diverse stimuli into compressed representations: complex states of affairs become remembered as compact biophysical engrams – this is the essence of the kind of modularity when a simple biophysical event kicks off the formation of a complex morphogenetic cascade such as building a “hand” in embryogenesis.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

claims.label: Animal senses use the same ion channel mechanisms found in bacteria
claims.statement: The senses of complex animals (touch, taste, temperature, hearing, etc.) are mediated by the same ion channel mechanisms that bacteria already used to sense their world.
claims.quote: Complex animals’ sense of touch, taste, temperature, hearing, etc. are mediated by the exact same ion channel mechanisms that were already discovered by bacteria and used to make sense of their world (Tasneem et al., 2005; Blackwell, 2006; Liebeskind et al., 2012; Nilius and Honore, 2012).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

claims.label: Cells in development minimize surprise and variational free energy like nervous systems
claims.statement: Living systems minimize surprise and optimize variational free energy by tuning internal states to best predict future stimuli, and this holds for individual cells during metazoan development as much as for nervous systems.
claims.quote: Systems minimize surprise and optimize variational free energy by tuning their internal states in a way that optimally predicts future stimuli (Friston and Ao, 2012; Friston, 2013; Badcock et al., 2019). This is as true for nervous systems as it is for individual cells during metazoan development (Friston et al., 2015; Ramstead et al., 2019).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

morpholib.note: Cells in the simulation minimise variational free energy during morphogenesis and regeneration, the mechanism the claim asserts.

morpholib.organism: Ambystoma mexicanum (axolotl salamander) regenerating forelimb

claims.label: Multicellularity and morphological complexity are driven by greedy infotaxis
claims.statement: Morphological complexity and multicellularity are proposed to be driven by greedy infotaxis: cells collecting as much information as possible from as far away in space and time as possible to minimize surprise, with greater network connectivity enlarging what the compound individual can sense, remember and store.
claims.quote: It is proposed that morphological complexity and multicellularity are driven by greedy infotaxis (Vergassola et al., 2007) – collecting as much information as possible, from as far away (in both space and time) as possible, to minimize surprise and optimize prediction.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

claims.label: Gap-junction coupling lets cells share sensing and form a larger Self
claims.statement: When cells are coupled into networks by gap junctions, the whole collective can measure and act on the same sensory data, so its Umwelt expands into a larger individual; physiological connectivity is thus the binding mechanism for larger unified Selves.
claims.quote: When coupled into networks via gap junctions however, the whole collective can measure and act upon the same sensory data – the Umwelt expands to create a larger individual in which the comprising cells share a unifying picture of the world (Figure 4).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

claims.label: Most anesthetics in plants and animals are gap junction uncouplers
claims.statement: Most anesthetics that remove cognition and sensory experience, in both plants and animals, act as gap junctional (bioelectric) uncouplers, which the author takes as consistent with connectivity binding cells into larger Selves.
claims.quote: It is thus no coincidence that most anesthetics used to remove cognition and sensory experience, whether in plants or animals, are gap junctional (bioelectric) uncouplers (Mantz et al., 1993; Wentlandt et al., 2006; Liu et al., 2012; Gremiaux et al., 2014; Baluska et al., 2016).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

claims.label: Swarms should show the same cognitive illusions as vertebrate brains
claims.statement: The proposed scale-invariant scaling of cognition predicts that swarm organisms should fall prey to the same kinds of cognitive illusions and failures of rationality as vertebrate brains, which the author says has been observed in ants and slime molds.
claims.quote: A prediction of this proposed scaling is that swarm organisms should fall prey to the same kinds of cognitive illusions and specific failures of rationality as do vertebrate brains, which has indeed been observed in ants and slime molds (Sakiyama and Gunji, 2013, 2016; Tani et al., 2014; Beekman and Latty, 2015).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

claims.label: Selves form only at intermediate levels of information sharing between subunits
claims.statement: Cognitive light cones grow or shrink as an agent's organization changes, and the key is a balance of selective information sharing through "synapses" (any structures that gate signals based on the state of others): too little sharing fails to bind subunits into a new Self, and too much yields an undifferentiated soup without modules or layered abstraction.
claims.quote: Too little sharing results in a failure to bind subunits into a new Self. Too much sharing results in a homogenous soup with insufficient differentiation of modules and abstraction of information across distinct layers.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Conclusion and Future Outlook

claims.label: Cancer is a reversible shrinking of a cell's computational boundary
claims.statement: Cancer is a reversible shrinking of the computational boundary of the Self: by becoming isolated from surrounding tissue's physiological (bioelectric) signals, a cell's cognitive boundary shrinks to its pre-multicellular, single-cell size, so it reverts to proliferating and migrating for its own benefit.
claims.quote: Cancer is a (reversible) shrinking of the computational boundary of a biosystem: by isolating itself from the surrounding tissue’s physiological signals, a cell’s cognitive boundary shrinks to the small size it had before multicellularity.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Conclusion and Future Outlook

claims.label: Agents scaled up from homeostatic loops by adding memory, anticipation and networks
claims.statement: Agents evolved by scaling up from basic homeostatic loops (whose set points are the first goals), driven by surprise minimization, through the successive addition of delays (memory), anticipation (inference), and spatially distributed networks that allow learning and abstraction.
claims.quote: Agents scaled up by evolving from basic homeostatic loops, driven by active inference (surprise minimization) via addition of delays (memory), anticipation (inference), and networks (spatially-distributed processing that enables learning and progressive abstraction/generalization from data).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Conclusion and Future Outlook

claims.label: Morphogenetic goal-directedness smooths the fitness landscape and boosts evolvability
claims.statement: Morphogenetic goal-directedness is a major evolutionary ratchet: because tissues adjust to reach the same anatomical goals despite changed conditions (e.g. muscle, vessels and tendons building a workable extra finger around an ectopic bone), it hides the disruptive effects of random mutations and smooths the anatomical fitness landscape.
claims.quote: Morphogenetic goal-directedness is a major evolutionary ratchet, smoothing the anatomical fitness landscape by hiding the otherwise potentially disruptive effects of random mutations.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Discussion

claims.label: Brains are not hardwired: ectopic tail eyes in tadpoles still support vision
claims.statement: Brains, like other developing organs, are not hardwired but can ascertain the body's structure and adjust their programs; tadpoles made to develop eyes on their tails, connected to the spinal cord rather than the brain, can still see quite well.
claims.quote: Tadpoles engineered to develop with eyes on their tails instead of in their usual spot can see quite well, despite the fact that the eyes connect to the spinal cord, not the brain (Blackiston and Levin, 2013; Blackiston et al., 2017). Brains, like other developing organs, are not hardwired but are able to ascertain the structure of the body and adjust their functional programs accordingly
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Discussion

claims.label: Editing bioelectric pattern set points can reprogram anatomy without genome editing
claims.statement: A better strategy for regenerative medicine than genetic rewiring of cells may be to edit the pattern-homeostatic set point and let wild-type cells build to it, as shown by altering bioelectric state in planaria to give permanently double-headed worms without genomic editing.
claims.quote: I have previously suggested that a better strategy than cellular re-wiring at the genetic level may be to edit the pattern-homeostatic set point and let wild-type cells build to the new spec. For example, the ability to re-write target morphology in planarian regeneration was recently shown, by altering the bioelectric state in flatworms, without genomic editing, giving rise to permanently double-headed worms (Durant et al., 2017; Levin et al., 2018).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Discussion

claims.label: Bioelectric circuits act as software: multistable states switched without genetic change
claims.statement: Ion channel and gap junction circuits are well suited to the "software" of life because they form feedback loops that implement dynamical systems with multiple attractors, which transient signals can switch between without changing the hardware (i.e. without mutating the DNA encoding the channels).
claims.quote: What makes electric circuits, whether ion channel-mediated or electronic, good for software is that they easily implement dynamical systems that have multiple attractors and can be made to occupy one physiological state or another by transient inputs (signals), not requiring changing the hardware (i.e., mutating the DNA encoding that hardware).
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Discussion

claims.label: Opiate addictiveness may derive from an ancient role in keeping cells together
claims.statement: If multicellularity arose from a drive to minimize predictive error, cells need a way to keep other cells nearby; this suggests the testable hypothesis that the addictive power of opiates and similar molecules derives from such ancient roots, which could be tested in early models of multicellularity and stem/somatic cell co-cultures.
claims.quote: Specifically, the implementation of multicellularity by the drive to minimize predictive error (Fields and Levin, 2019) suggests that cells need a way to keep other cells nearby. This suggests the testable hypothesis that the addictive power of opiates and similar molecules derives from such ancient roots.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Predictions and Research Program

claims.label: Forced electrogenic and gap junction expression could make unicells form bodies
claims.statement: The proposed role of bioelectrics in multicellularity predicts that forcing expression of appropriate electrogenic proteins and gap junctions in a unicellular organism should induce metazoan-like bodies, and that appropriate changes of bioelectric dynamics may dissolve a metazoan body.
claims.quote: The proposed crucial role of bioelectrics in multicellularity predicts that it should be possible to induce the formation of metazoan-like bodies in an otherwise unicellular organism by forcing the expression of appropriate electrogenic proteins and gap junctions. Similarly, it may be possible to induce dissolution of an entire metazoan body by appropriate changes of bioelectric dynamics.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Predictions and Research Program

claims.label: Regeneration across kingdoms should consistently use electrogenic proteins
claims.statement: Bioelectrics should be widely conserved in regeneration across kingdoms: transcriptomes of regeneration from damaged bacterial biofilms to plants to animal limb and organ regeneration should show consistent use of electrogenic proteins, and neurotransmitter signalling should be conserved enough that cognitive-modulator drugs affect biofilms and Physarum.
claims.quote: Bioelectrics should be widely conserved in regeneration across Kingdoms; transcriptomic analyses of regeneration events from damaged bacterial biofilms to plants to metazoan models of limb and organ regeneration should all show consistent use of electrogenic proteins in the events that enable cooperation toward self-limiting morphogenetic cascades.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Predictions and Research Program

claims.label: Cells and tissues may have something it is like to make decisions
claims.statement: Because some nervous systems give rise to first-person experience and neural and non-neural networks differ minimally apart from time scale, it is natural to hypothesize that there is something it is like to be a tissue or organ making decisions, e.g. a pancreas may have as much proto-consciousness as a simple neural network.
claims.quote: But, given that at least some nervous systems do give rise to such experience and that the differences between neural networks and non-neural ones (aside from temporal scale) are minimal, it is natural to hypothesize that there is something-it-is-like to being a tissue or organ and making decisions.
claims.work: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition
claims.chapter: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › What Does It Feel Like to be a Pancreas?

claims.label: Evolutionary algorithms can design novel living organisms built from frog cells
claims.statement: A pipeline in which an evolutionary algorithm designs candidate organisms in silico for a desired function, and transferable designs are then built from Xenopus cells with a cell-based construction toolkit, can produce novel living systems that show the predicted behaviours, though some steps still need manual intervention.
claims.quote: Here we show a scalable pipeline for creating functional novel lifeforms: AI methods automatically design diverse candidate lifeforms in silico to perform some desired function, and transferable designs are then created using a cell-based construction toolkit to realize living systems with the predicted behaviors.
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Abstract

claims.label: Designed organisms moved as simulated when upright, much less when inverted
claims.statement: For at least one deciliated, cardiac-muscle-powered design, the upright organisms' direction of movement matched that of the in silico design under random perturbations, and inverting the design significantly reduced net displacement both in silico and in vivo.
claims.quote: More specifically, the upright organisms’ direction of movement matched that of the in silico design under random perturbations (P < 0.01; details in SI Appendix, section S9), and inverting the design significantly reduced its net displacement both in silico (P < 0.001) and in vivo (P < 0.0001).

claims.label: Behaviour transfer from simulation to organism was due to the designed shape
claims.statement: The authors interpret the orientation-dependent match between simulated and living organisms as showing that successful transfer of locomotion from simulation to the living organism was due to the designed morphology itself, not chance.
claims.quote: This suggests that successful transference did not result by chance but rather was due to the design itself.
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Results › Locomotion.

claims.label: Motile designs spontaneously aggregate particles in simulation and in vivo
claims.statement: When the environment contains particulate matter, motile designs spontaneously gather the particles into aggregates, both in simulation and as living Xenopus-cell organisms.
claims.quote: When the environment is strewn with particulate matter, motile designs spontaneously aggregate the external objects both in silico (SI Appendix, Fig. S10) and in vivo (Fig. 3F and SI Appendix, Fig. S11).
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Results › Object Manipulation.

claims.label: Pairs of organisms collide, bond and orbit, more so with cilia active
claims.statement: Collective behaviours predicted in simulation were observed in vivo: two organisms often collide, form a temporary mechanical bond and orbit each other for several revolutions before detaching, and this is more pronounced when cilia are not inhibited.
claims.quote: For instance, two designs often collide, form a temporary mechanical bond, and orbit about each other for several revolutions before detaching along tangential trajectories (SI Appendix, Fig. S10). This phenomenon is more pronounced when cilia are not inhibited on the organisms
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Results › Collective Behavior.

claims.label: Selection for locomotion under random actuation evolved derandomizing shapes
claims.statement: In the voxel-based soft-body simulation with randomly phased contractile cells, selection for locomotion produced morphologies that derandomize motion: shape and the distribution of passive and contractile cells evolved so the global movement was coherent despite random actuation.
claims.quote: As a side effect of selection pressure for locomotion, derandomizing morphologies evolved: evolutionary improvement occurred through changes in overall shape, and distribution of the passive and contractile cells, to collectively derandomize the global movement produced by the random actuation.
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

claims.label: Cell competence lets neural-less novel aggregates self-organize functionally
claims.statement: The behavioural competence of individual cells and their propensity to cooperate in groups facilitate functional morphogenesis in novel circumstances, so that the designed organisms, despite lacking nervous systems, following novel developmental trajectories and mixing tissues, still possess self-organizing properties that support their designed behaviour.
claims.quote: The behavioral competence of individual cells, and the propensity of cells to cooperate in groups, facilitate functional morphogenesis in novel circumstances. The lifeforms presented here, despite lacking nervous systems, following novel developmental trajectories, and being composed of materials from different tissues, nevertheless possess these self-organizing properties.
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

claims.label: Cardiomyocytes in built organisms spontaneously made phase-matched contractions
claims.statement: Although signalling between cardiomyocytes was not designed or enforced, cardiac muscle cells in the built organisms spontaneously coordinated to produce coherent, phase-matched contractions that aided locomotion.
claims.quote: For instance, although signaling between cardiomyocytes was not enforced, emergent spontaneous coordination among the cardiac muscle cells produced coherent, phase-matched contractions which aided locomotion in the physically realized designs.
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Discussion

claims.label: Reconfigurable organisms self-repair, closing lacerations
claims.statement: Reconfigurable organisms built from Xenopus cells maintain their externally imposed shape and also self-repair after damage, for example automatically closing lacerations.
claims.quote: Finally, reconfigurable organisms not only self-maintain their externally imposed configuration, but they also self-repair in the face of damage, such as automatically closing lacerations (SI Appendix, Fig. S9).
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

claims.label: Adding hydrodynamics and random actuation made simulated gaits match living ones
claims.statement: Designs first evolved on simulated land had bounding gaits that did not transfer to living organisms; adding first-order hydrodynamics and randomized phase offsets produced designs whose behaviour better matched the living systems, in contact with the ground for 93.3% of evaluation versus 52.7% on the first pass.
claims.quote: The behavior of designs generated on the second pass better matched the behavior of the actual living systems: on average, designs were in contact with the ground plane for 93.3% of their evaluation period, compared to just 52.7% on the first pass (SI Appendix, section S6).
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Materials and Methods › Evolutionary Design.

claims.label: Shape concavities of 100 µm or more persist in developing stem cell aggregates
claims.statement: Aggregates of developing Xenopus pluripotent cells tend to close small gaps in their geometry; concavities 100 µm wide or more (12% of body length) gave stable long-term deformations, setting the minimal buildable feature size.
claims.quote: Preliminary work determined that concavities with a width of 100 µm or greater (12% of total body length) produced stable long-term deformations suitable for biological building (SI Appendix, Fig. S7).
claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Materials and Methods › Build Filter.

claims.label: All known cognitive agents are collective intelligences made of agential parts
claims.statement: Every known cognitive agent is a collective intelligence: biological agents are made of parts (cells and other components) that are themselves agents in important ways, and there is no truly indivisible cognitive being.
claims.quote: All known cognitive agents are collective intelligences, because we are all made of parts; biological agents in particular are not just structurally modular, but made of parts that are themselves agents in important ways.
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Introduction

claims.label: Memories can persist through complete brain regeneration in planaria
claims.statement: In some organisms such as planaria, memories (prior knowledge and behavioural tendencies) can apparently persist after the complete regeneration of the brain, being transferred onto the newly constructed brain.
claims.quote: Not only that, but memories can apparently persist following the complete regeneration of brains in some organisms (McConnell et al., 1959; Corning, 1966; Shomrat and Levin, 2013) such as planaria, in which prior knowledge and behavioral tendencies are somehow transferred onto a newly-constructed brain.
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Cognition: Changing the Subject

claims.label: Tadpoles with eyes on their tails can still perform visual learning
claims.statement: Xenopus tadpoles engineered to have eyes on their tails instead of their heads are still readily able to perform visual learning tasks, illustrating that minds readily adapt to radically altered body architectures.
claims.quote: When tadpoles are created to have eyes on their tails, instead of their heads, they are still readily able to perform visual learning tasks (Blackiston and Levin, 2013; Blackiston et al., 2017).
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Cognition: Changing the Subject

claims.label: Transitions in cognitive capacity are gradual, not binary
claims.statement: Although major differences in cognitive function exist among diverse intelligences, transitions between them have not been shown to be binary or rapid relative to the timescale of individual agents; cognition-related properties form a continuum from humble proto-cognitive systems to advanced minds.
claims.quote: Specifically, while major differences in cognitive function of course exist among diverse intelligences, transitions between them have not been shown to be binary or rapid relative to the timescale of individual agents.
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Philosophical Foundations of an Approach to Diverse Intelligences

claims.label: A system's level of agency must be determined empirically by prediction and control
claims.statement: Under TAME, how much agency a system has is an empirical, observer-dependent question: the correct level of agency to attribute is the one whose model and intervention strategy give the most efficient prediction and control of the system, as established by experiment.
claims.quote: Thus, the correct level of agency with which to treat any system must be determined by experiments that reveal which kind of model and strategy provides the most efficient predictive and control capability over the system.
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Philosophical Foundations of an Approach to Diverse Intelligences

claims.label: Gene regulatory network models exhibit associative learning
claims.statement: Analyses of biological gene regulatory network models show that they exhibit associative and several other kinds of learning, as well as pattern completion and generalization, suggesting GRNs could be trained with patterned stimuli rather than rewired.
claims.quote: Indeed, recent analyses of biological GRN models reveal that they exhibit associative and several other kinds of learning capacity, as well as pattern completion and generalization (Watson et al., 2010, 2014; Szilagyi et al., 2020; Biswas et al., 2021).
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Philosophical Foundations of an Approach to Diverse Intelligences

claims.label: A Self is marked by goals, compound memories and credit assignment above its parts
claims.statement: TAME defines the hallmarks of a Self as the ability to pursue goals, to own compound (e.g. associative) memories, and to serve as the locus of credit assignment (reward or punishment), each at a scale larger than any of its components can achieve alone.
claims.quote: The TAME framework takes the following as the basic hallmarks of being a Self: the ability to pursue goals, to own compound (e.g., associative) memories, and to serve as the locus for credit assignment (be rewarded or punished), where all of these are at a scale larger than possible for any of its components alone.
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework

claims.label: The spatiotemporal scale of an agent's goals delineates its Self (cognitive light cone)
claims.statement: Selves can be classified and compared by the spatio-temporal scale of the goals they can represent and work toward (their 'cognitive light cone'), and this scale delineates the boundaries of each Self.
claims.quote: Specifically (Figure 4), a “space-time” diagram can be created where the spatio-temporal scale of any agent’s goals delineates that Self and its cognitive boundaries.
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework

claims.label: Stress binds distributed modules into one larger homeostatic loop
claims.statement: Stress, defined as a system-level response to the difference between current state and a setpoint, scales Selves by binding modules that sense and act at different scales and locations into one global homeostatic loop; propagated stress signals recruit distant sub-agents to act so as to reduce their own stress.
claims.quote: Stress is a systemic response to a difference between current state and a desired setpoint; it is an essential component to scaling of Selves because it enables different modules (which sense and act on things at different scales and in distributed locations) to be bound together in one global homeostatic loop (toward a larger purpose).

claims.label: Behavioural problem-solving in 3D space derives from older problem-solving in other spaces
claims.statement: Problem-solving behaviour of animals in three-dimensional space is proposed to be a variant of an evolutionarily more ancient capacity to solve problems in metabolic, physiological, transcriptional and morphogenetic spaces.
claims.quote: It is proposed that the traditional problem-solving behavior we see in standard animals in 3D space is just a variant of evolutionarily more ancient capacity to solve problems in metabolic, physiological, transcriptional, and morphogenetic spaces (as one possible sequential timeline along which evolution pivoted some of the same strategies to solve problems in new spaces).

claims.label: Planaria regenerate barium-insensitive heads after barium-induced head loss
claims.statement: Planaria exposed to barium, a non-specific potassium channel blocker, lose their heads but soon regenerate heads that are completely insensitive to barium, by transcriptionally regulating relatively few genes; the authors interpret this as cells navigating transcriptional space to solve a novel physiological stressor not met in evolution.
claims.quote: For example, when planaria are exposed to barium, a non-specific potassium channel blocker, their heads explode. Remarkably, they soon regenerate heads that are completely insensitive to barium (Emmons-Bell et al., 2019).

claims.label: Picasso tadpoles with scrambled faces become largely normal frogs
claims.statement: Xenopus tadpoles whose craniofacial organs were placed in abnormal positions ('Picasso tadpoles') tend to become largely normal frogs, because the organs move along novel, abnormal paths and stop at the correct frog-face positions, showing that craniofacial remodelling is goal-directed rather than hardwired.
claims.quote: Amazingly, they tend to turn into largely normal frogs because the craniofacial organs move in novel, abnormal paths [sometimes overshooting and needing to return a bit (Pinet et al., 2019)] and stop when they get to the correct frog face positions.

claims.label: Deer antler trophic memory is a rewritable pattern memory
claims.statement: In deer, a wound made on a branched antler in one year leads to ectopic tines at the same location in later years after the antler is shed, which the author interprets as an experience-dependent, rewritable pattern memory in which the target morphology is rewritten without changing the genome.
claims.quote: This is an example of experience-dependent, re-writable pattern memory, in which the target morphology (the setpoint for anatomical homeostasis) is re-written within standard hardware.

claims.label: Altering planarian voltage patterns changes head number and head species-shape
claims.statement: In planaria, manipulating the endogenous bioelectric voltage pattern by targeting gap junctions or ion channels can produce worms with one, two or zero heads, or with head and brain shapes resembling other extant planarian species.
claims.quote: Manipulation of the normal voltage pattern by targeting the gap junctions (Sordillo and Bargmann, 2021) or ion channels can give rise to planaria with one, two, or 0 heads, or heads with shape (and brain shape) resembling other extant species of planaria (Emmons-Bell et al., 2015; Sullivan et al., 2016).

claims.label: Two-headed planarian state persists through further cutting despite wild-type genome
claims.statement: Planaria with abnormal head number induced by transient bioelectric manipulation are permanently altered: when cut into pieces with no further treatment, the pieces continue to regenerate with abnormal head number despite wild-type genetics.
claims.quote: Remarkably, the worms with abnormal head number are permanently altered to this pattern, despite their wild-type genetics: cut into pieces with no further manipulations, the pieces continue to regenerate with abnormal head number (Oviedo et al., 2010; Durant et al., 2017).

claims.label: Transient bioelectric states can rewrite false pattern memories in animals
claims.statement: Modulating a transient bioelectric state is a conserved mechanism by which false pattern memories (altered target morphologies) can be written into the genetically specified electrical circuits of a living animal, analogous to incepting false behavioural memories in brains with optogenetics.
claims.quote: Thus, much like the optogenetic techniques used to incept false behavioral memories into brains (Vetere et al., 2019), modulation of transient bioelectric state is a conserved mechanism by which false pattern memories can be re-written into the genetically-specified electrical circuits of a living animal.

claims.label: Newt kidney tubules keep correct lumen size when cell size changes
claims.statement: Newt kidney tubules normally made of 8 to 10 cells in cross-section are built from fewer cells when cell size is experimentally enlarged, and from a single cell wrapping around itself when cells are made very large, showing that different molecular mechanisms (cell-cell interactions vs cytoskeletal deformation) can be deployed to reach the same anatomical outcome.
claims.quote: Even more remarkable than the scaling of the cell number to unexpected size changes (on an ontogenetic, not evolutionary, timescale) is the fact that if the cells are made really huge, just one cell wraps around itself and still makes a proper lumen (Figure 6D).
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

claims.label: Injury to one limb can be read out from the opposite limb within 30 seconds
claims.statement: Limbs show mirror-neuron-like and somatotopic responses to injury outside the nervous system: the type and site of damage to one limb can be read out within 30 seconds by imaging the opposite, uninjured limb.
claims.quote: For example, mirror neurons and somatotopic representation are seen in limbs’ response to injury, where the type and site of damage to one limb can be read out within 30 s from imaging the opposite, un-injured limbs (Busse et al., 2018).
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

claims.label: Genes for morphogenesis and for learning and memory should overlap widely
claims.statement: TAME predicts significant and specific overlap between genes involved in morphogenesis and genes in memory and learning categories, beyond the known shared ion channels, connexins and neurotransmitter machinery; it also predicts that memory genes will appear in genetic studies of cancer, regeneration and embryogenesis.
claims.quote: Significant and specific overlap are predicted for genes involved in morphogenesis and cognition (categories of memory and learning).
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

test_contract.expected_observation: Pre-registered: after exclusions, (a) the one-sided Fisher exact test of overlap between the learning-or-memory set (GO:0007611 and is_a/part_of descendants) and the morphogenesis set (GO:0009653 and descendants) gives odds ratio > 1.5 and p < 0.001; (b) the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio stratified by deciles of each gene's number of experimental BP annotations is > 1.5; (c) the unstratified odds ratio is above the 75th percentile of odds ratios between the morphogenesis set and every control BP term whose post-exclusion gene count is within a factor of 1.5 of the learning-or-memory set's and which is neither an ancestor nor a descendant of GO:0007611 or GO:0009653.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Pre-registered: unstratified odds ratio <= 1.2 or p >= 0.05, or Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio <= 1.2, or the odds ratio at or below the median of the size-matched control terms. Outcomes meeting neither criterion are pre-registered as 'mixed' (overlap present but not specific, or explained by annotation depth).
test_contract.inference_method: fetch.py downloads go-basic.obo and the MGI GAF. analysis.py drops NOT-qualified and obsolete-term lines, builds each gene's set of experimental BP terms and their is_a/part_of ancestors, removes 612 genes annotated to ion channel, gap junction or neurotransmission terms, and tests overlap of GO:0007611 and GO:0009653 in the remaining 10,243 genes with a one-sided Fisher exact test. Annotation depth is controlled by a Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio over ten equal-sized strata of genes ranked by their number of distinct experimental BP terms. Specificity is the percentile of the odds ratio among the 327 BP terms of 128-286 genes that are neither ancestors nor descendants of either term.

claims.label: Morphogenesis should be trainable by reinforcement for specific anatomical outcomes
claims.statement: TAME predicts (not yet tested) that the collective intelligence of tissues may be trainable by reinforcement learning, using rewards and punishments such as nutrients, endorphins or shock, to produce specific morphological or gene-expression outcomes.
claims.quote: Another key prediction that remains to be tested (ongoing in our lab) is trainability of morphogenesis. The collective intelligence of tissues could be sophisticated enough to be trainable via reinforcement learning for specific morphological outcomes.

claims.label: Voltage-sensitive channels and gap junctions form rewritable dynamical memories
claims.statement: Because ion channels and gap junctions are themselves voltage-sensitive, a transient voltage state can trigger progressive depolarization or gap-junction closure, so non-neural bioelectric circuits readily form dynamical-system memories that store information and change computation without changing the channel or junction hardware.
claims.quote: The fact that a transient voltage state passing through a cell can set off a cycle of progressive depolarization (like an action potential) or gap junctional (GJ) closure means that such circuits readily form dynamical systems memories which can store different information and change their computational behavior without changing the hardware
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

claims.label: Gap junctions merge cells into a larger Self by erasing signal ownership
claims.statement: Because signals passing through gap junctions carry no marker of their cell of origin, gap-junctional coupling partially erases informational (memory) boundaries between cells, which promotes the formation of a larger Self whose parts work toward common goals.
claims.quote: Thus, this property of GJ coupling promotes the creation of a larger Self by partially erasing the mnemic boundaries between the parts which might impair their ability to work toward a common goal.
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
