claims.label: Cancer is a shrinking of the Self after gap junction closure
claims.statement: Oncogene expression and carcinogen exposure close gap junctions, and the consequence is transformation to cancer, in which cells revert to unicellular-like selves, shrink their computational boundaries and treat the rest of the body as external environment.
claims.quote: Indeed this occurs in cancer, where oncogene expression and carcinogen exposure leads to a closure of GJs (Vine and Bertram, 2002; Leithe et al., 2006). The consequence of this is transformation to cancer, where cells revert to their ancient unicellular selves (Levin, 2021b)—shrinking their computational boundaries and treating the rest of the body as external environment.
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › A Bioelectric Model of the Scaling of the Self

claims.label: Managing bioelectric connectivity induces or suppresses cancer independent of genetics
claims.statement: Managing bioelectric connectivity between cells can override genetically determined states, inducing metastatic melanoma in a wild-type background or suppressing tumorigenesis driven by strong oncogenes such as p53 or KRAS mutations, so genetic alterations are not necessary either to induce or to revert cancer.
claims.quote: Indeed, recent data show that managing this connectivity can override default genetically-determined states, inducing metastatic melanoma in a perfectly wild-type background (Blackiston et al., 2011) or suppressing tumorigenesis induced by strong oncogenes like p53 or KRAS mutations (Chernet and Levin, 2013a,b).
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › A Bioelectric Model of the Scaling of the Self

claims.label: Developmental bioelectricity preceded and gave rise to nervous systems
claims.statement: Developmental bioelectrics is an ancient precursor of nervous systems: evolution first used analog bioelectric dynamics to position body configuration in developmental morphospace, long before some cells specialized in fast digital spiking to control behaviour in 3D space.
claims.quote: Evolution first exploited this to enable cell groups to position the body configuration in developmental morphospace, long before some cells specialized to use very fast, digital spiking as neural networks for control of behavior as movement in 3-dimensional space (Fields et al., 2020).
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems

claims.label: Context-sensitive ion channels appear alongside complex metazoan body plans
claims.statement: Ion channel phylogeny is ancient (many channel families likely predate the most recent unicellular ancestor of animals), and the appearance of context-sensitive channels enabling new bioelectric feedback loops tracks the appearance of complex body plans at the emergence of metazoa, indicating an evolutionary continuum from single-cell excitability to cognition via somatic pattern control.
claims.quote: The phylogeny of ion channels is ancient, and the appearance of context-sensitive channels (enabling new kinds of bioelectrical feedback loops) tracks well with the appearance of complex body plans at the emergence of metazoa (Moran et al., 2015), revealing the remarkable evolutionary continuum that leads from membrane excitability in single cells to cognitive functions in advanced organisms, by way of somatic pattern control (Cook et al., 2014).
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems

claims.label: A single ion channel can induce complete ectopic eyes where Pax6 cannot
claims.statement: In Xenopus, the action of a single ion channel can induce an eye-specific bioelectric state that creates complete eyes in gut endoderm, spinal cord and posterior tissues, locations where genetic master regulators such as Pax6 are insufficient in vertebrates; bioelectric states thus act as master regulators that evolution can exploit for modular anatomical change.
claims.quote: For example, the action of a single ion channel can induce an eye-specific bioelectric state that creates complete eyes in gut endoderm, spinal cord, and posterior tissues (Pai et al., 2012)—locations where genetic “master regulators” like the Pax6 transcription factor are insufficient in vertebrates (Chow et al., 1999).
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems

claims.label: Mutations in electrogenic genes can produce coordinated, long-range anatomical change
claims.statement: Because the same membrane-voltage dynamics can be produced by many ion-channel combinations and bioelectric states act across tissue distances, evolution can swap channels freely, and simple mutations in electrogenic genes can cause long-range, highly coordinated changes in anatomy (supported by KCNH8 and a connexin in an evolutionary shift of fish fin morphology).
claims.quote: evolution is free to swap out channels and explore the bioelectrical state space: simple mutations in electrogenic genes can exert very long-range, highly coordinated changes in anatomy.
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems

claims.label: Multiscale competency shields mutations from selection and smooths fitness landscapes
claims.statement: In organisms with a multiscale competency architecture, whose modules actively correct toward a target morphology, mutations that would be detrimental in hardwired organisms (e.g. displacing the eye) become neutral, so the architecture shields some of mutations' negative effects from selection and smooths the fitness landscape.
claims.quote: Thus, MCA shields from selection some aspects of mutations’ negative effects (which inevitably are the bulk of random mutations’ consequences).
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Evolutionary Aspects › Multi-Scale Autonomy Potentiates the Speed of Evolution

claims.label: Anatomical homeostasis may exist mainly to correct mutation-induced deviations
claims.statement: The primary reason for anatomical homeostasis in regulative development and regeneration may be to correct deviations from target morphology caused by mutations, rather than to repair damage.
claims.quote: The primary reason for the anatomical homeostasis seen in regulative development and regeneration may be for dealing, not with damage, but with deviations from target morphology induced by mutations.
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Evolutionary Aspects › Multi-Scale Autonomy Potentiates the Speed of Evolution

claims.label: Systems operating in morphogenetic or transcriptional spaces have minimal consciousness
claims.statement: TAME provisionally holds that consciousness comes in degrees and that embodiment includes perception-action systems in any space, implying that systems operating in morphogenetic, transcriptional and other spaces should have some, if very minimal, degree of consciousness.
claims.quote: This implies, counter to many people’s intuitions, that systems that operate in morphogenetic, transcriptional, and other spaces should also have some (if very minimal) degree of consciousness.
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Consciousness

claims.label: General anesthetics block gap junctions, dissolving the higher-level Self
claims.statement: General anesthetics are gap-junction blockers, and on TAME's account shutting down electrical communication between cells makes the higher-level computational layer (the larger Self) disappear while the cells remain healthy; gap-junction blockers anesthetize organisms ranging from plants and Hydra to humans.
claims.quote: Interestingly, general anesthetics are gap junction blockers (Wentlandt et al., 2006): consistent with the cognitive scaling example above, shutting down electrical communication among the cells leads to a disappearance of the higher-level computational layer while the cellular network is disrupted.
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Consciousness

claims.label: Briefly gap-junction-blocked planaria make other species' heads, then revert
claims.statement: Planaria briefly treated with a gap-junction blocker regenerate heads shaped like those of other planarian species but eventually remodel back to their correct species-specific target morphology, which the author takes as parallel to the temporary loss and return of the Self under anesthesia.
claims.quote: Interestingly, and in line with the proposed isomorphism between cognition and morphogenesis, gap junction blockade has exactly this effect in regeneration: planaria briefly treated with GJ blocker regenerate heads of other species, but eventually snap out of it and remodel back to their correct target morphology (Emmons-Bell et al., 2015).
claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Consciousness

claims.label: Published ODE models of gene and protein pathways show several kinds of memory
claims.statement: In simulations of 35 published ODE models of gene regulatory networks and protein/metabolic pathways from BioModels, the networks show several distinct kinds of memory (UCS-based, pairing, transfer, associative and consolidation memory) in response to patterns of node stimulation.
claims.quote: Here, we characterize biological gene regulatory circuit models and protein pathways and find them capable of several different kinds of memory.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › Abstract

claims.label: Biological pathway models have more memory than structurally matched random networks
claims.statement: Compared with 500 random gene-circuit networks matched to the biological models in size, edges, degree, betweenness, PageRank and hubness, the biological ODE pathway models show higher prevalence of most memory types, fewer no-memory cases, and more correlated memory types, indicating that generic network dynamics are not solely responsible for trainability.
claims.quote: Random networks do not show similar memory behavior as models of biological processes, indicating that generic network dynamics are not solely responsible for trainability.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › Abstract

claims.label: Behaviour-shaping of pathways could be an alternative to gene therapy
claims.statement: Rational stimulation regimes derived from computational models of pathway memory could control pathway function without genomic editing or network rewiring, so behaviour-shaping of pathway responses stands as a potential biomedical alternative to gene therapy (e.g. to counter drug pharmacoresistance and sensitization).
claims.quote: Rational control of dynamic pathway function using stimuli derived from computational models opens the door to empirical studies of proto-cognitive capacities in unconventional embodiments and suggests numerous possible applications in biomedicine, where behavior shaping of pathway responses stand as a potential alternative to gene therapy.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › Abstract

claims.label: Memory is defined functionally as future behaviour modulated by past experience
claims.statement: In the basal cognition framework adopted by Biswas, Clawson and Levin, memory is defined in substrate-independent functionalist terms: a system has memory when its future behaviour is specifically modulated by its past experience, which allows the question of whether molecular networks such as gene regulatory networks are trainable.
claims.quote: Consistent with the basal cognition paradigm, we define memory in functionalist terms—a system in which future behavior is specifically modulated by past experience.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 1. Introduction

claims.label: Nearly all surveyed pathway models have memory; very small networks may not
claims.statement: Memory was found in all but four of the 35 surveyed BioModels pathway models, and three of those four had fewer than four nodes, suggesting that very small networks either cannot have, or are very unlikely to have, memory.
claims.quote: Overall, we found memory models in all surveyed biological networks except four models, of which three had a low number of nodes (<4) suggesting that too small networks either cannot, or are very unlikely to, have memory
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.1. Biological Networks May Possess Multiple Types of Memory

claims.label: No simple network-topology measure predicts memory in pathway models
claims.statement: Across the 35 surveyed BioModels pathway models, the amount of memory showed no significant correlation with mean number of nodes, edges, degree or hubness, so no single network property is indicative of memory.
claims.quote: Additionally, we tested to see if certain network properties, such as mean number of nodes, edges, degree, and hubness were associated with more or less memory and found there were no significant correlations with any of these measures and any memory (see Discussion).
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.1. Biological Networks May Possess Multiple Types of Memory

claims.label: Feedback loops may be conducive to pathway memory but are not the only route
claims.statement: Self-sustaining feedback loops with hysteresis, such as the positive-feedback dual phosphorylation–dephosphorylation cycle of MAPK, may be conducive to memory in biochemical networks, but feedback loop architecture may be only one of many ways to support such memories.
claims.quote: Overall, we suggest that feedback loop network architecture may be conducive to memories but may be only one way of many to support them.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.1. Biological Networks May Possess Multiple Types of Memory

claims.label: Pathway memories can form through dynamics alone, without structural change
claims.statement: In ODE models of biological pathways, memories (such as associative memory, in which a neutral stimulus becomes a conditioned stimulus) can be formed by patterns of stimulation through dynamical interactions alone, without changing the network's structure or parameters.
claims.quote: Again, while feedback loop architecture is present, our results indicate that memories can be formed through dynamical interactions alone, without changing network structure/architecture.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.1. Biological Networks May Possess Multiple Types of Memory

claims.label: Pathway-model memories are robust to a wide range of stimulus strengths
claims.statement: In the surveyed ODE pathway models, memory formation is robust to training stimuli of 10x, 50x and 100x baseline (most models kept the same number of memories and only 10% lost memories), and some models formed more memories with weaker stimulation.
claims.quote: We conclude that the memory properties are robust to a wide range of stimulus strengths, a desirable property for therapeutics, and also for functional linkages with other cell pathways during evolution.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.2. Memory Effects Are Robust to Different Strengths of Stimulus

claims.label: Noise increases memory in pathway models, especially associative memory
claims.statement: Adding stochastic noise to simulations of the surveyed ODE pathway models left memories intact in most models (83%) and increased memory overall by about 20%, most notably associative memory, suggesting that biological noise does not inhibit and may help the trainability of such networks.
claims.quote: Interestingly, while almost all models retained the memories created (83%), there was an overall 20% increase in memory in the presence of noise (averaged across models and memory phenotypes) most notably in the associative memory paradigm.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.3. Memory Effects Are Robust to Noise

claims.label: Most pathway-model memories persist over long periods and survive recall
claims.statement: In the surveyed ODE pathway models with UCS-based memory, most networks retain the bulk of their memories over waiting periods up to 100 times the initial one, and testing (recalling) a memory generally does not destroy it and in rare cases strengthens it.
claims.quote: Overall, we conclude that while some networks have a limit on how long they retain training, the majority of networks can retain the bulk of their possible memories over very long time periods and that in general, memory ‘access’ does not destroy the memory but can, in some rare cases, increase memory.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.4. Memory Effects Are Stable over Long Periods

claims.label: Serially trained associative memories cause catastrophic forgetting in pathway models
claims.statement: When two associative memories are trained one after another in ODE pathway models, all biological and random models show catastrophic forgetting in which both memories are lost, whereas two UCS-based memories can be stored serially or in parallel.
claims.quote: When more complex memories were tested, here AM-AM memory pairs, when created serially all biological and random models showed catastrophic forgetting wherein both are lost.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.5. Can Networks Be Trained to Keep More Than One Memory?

claims.label: Pathway memory is distributed uniformly across organism classes
claims.statement: Memory in the surveyed pathway models shows no privileged association with any class of organism (bacteria, slime mould, yeast, plants, lower vertebrates, mammals), being distributed roughly uniformly, which may suggest that proto-cognitive capacity is found across many strata of life.
claims.quote: We found no privileged categorization of memory over classes of organisms—memory seemed distributed uniformly over all strata of life (see Figure S3).
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.5. Can Networks Be Trained to Keep More Than One Memory?

claims.label: Habituation (pharmacoresistance) occurs in every testable pathway model
claims.statement: Modelling pharmacoresistance as habituation (a progressive 50% drop in response across repeated, lengthening stimulations), at least one habituating stimulus–response pair was found in each of the 27 testable BioModels pathway models, with 1–50% of node pairs per model habituating.
claims.quote: Overall, we were able to test 27 out of the 35 models (77%, see Section 4) and at least one instance of habituation was found for each model, with the distribution of pharmacoresistance across all potential models ranging between 1–50% (see Figure 8 and Figures S11–S13).
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.7. Making and Breaking Pharmacoresistance

claims.label: Pharmacoresistance may be an evolved form of network adaptation
claims.statement: Because random ODE networks rarely show habituation in more than 30% of stimulus–response pairs while biological pathway models differ from that distribution, pharmacoresistance (habituation) may be a form of network adaptation more prevalent in networks shaped by evolutionary pressure, not due to network properties alone.
claims.quote: This would hint that pharmacoresistance may be a form of network adaptation, which would indeed be more prevalent in a biological network shaped by evolutionary pressure.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.7. Making and Breaking Pharmacoresistance

claims.label: Stimulating other nodes can break pharmacoresistance in many pathway models
claims.statement: In 17 of the 27 habituating BioModels pathway models (about 63%), stimulating a third node (neither the stimulus nor the response) abolished habituation for some stimulus–response pairs, so some biological networks contain discoverable stimulus nodes that may serve to break pharmacoresistance without rewiring the network.
claims.quote: Overall, we conclude that in some biological networks, there are discoverable stimulus nodes that may serve towards breaking pharmacoresistance.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.7. Making and Breaking Pharmacoresistance

claims.label: Sensitization is common in biological pathway models but rare in random networks
claims.statement: Sensitization (a progressive 1.5-fold increase in response over repeated stimulations) was found in 27 of the 35 BioModels pathway models, whereas very few random gene-circuit models showed it (under 10% of pairings per model), suggesting the feature may be unique to biology or require more complex random models.
claims.quote: Interestingly, very few of the random models had UCS-R relations that generated sensitization (<10% of UCS-R pairings per model), indicating that this feature may be unique to biology, or that more complex random models would be needed to find such behavior (Figure 10 and Figures S17–S19).
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.8. Making and Breaking Sensitization

claims.label: Sensitization is harder to break than habituation in pathway models
claims.statement: In ODE pathway models, sensitization could be broken by stimulating a third node in only 8 of 27 sensitizing models, mostly for fewer than 5% of node pairs, so breaking sensitization is less likely than breaking habituation and therapies may need other avenues of intervention.
claims.quote: Overall, we conclude that while sensitization is prevalent in biological models, the breaking of sensitization is less likely than in habituation, and therefore therapeutic models may need to pursue other avenues of intervention.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.8. Making and Breaking Sensitization

claims.label: Standard topology measures are likely insufficient to design or evolve memory
claims.statement: Because random networks matched to biological pathway models in number of nodes, edges, indegree, outdegree, betweenness, PageRank and hubness lack comparable memory, those structural features are not likely to be sufficient criteria for designing or evolving networks with memories.
claims.quote: Interestingly, since the random networks were designed to match the biological models in number of nodes, number of edges, indegree, outdegree, betweenness, PageRank, and hubness, those features are not likely to be sufficient criteria for designing (or evolving) networks with memories.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 3. Discussion

claims.label: Oscillatory pathway networks may gain more memory from noise
claims.statement: Biswas, Clawson and Levin hypothesize that biological networks with strong oscillatory components (such as cell-cycle, circadian-clock and developmental-timer models) may benefit more from noise in terms of memory, analogous to harmonic resonance, though some oscillatory models did not show this.
claims.quote: From this, we hypothesize that biological networks with strong oscillatory components may benefit more, from a memory perspective, to noise, similar to the case of harmonic resonance [122].
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 3. Discussion

claims.label: Pathway memory is more robust to edge perturbation, perhaps from selection
claims.statement: The memory capacity of biological ODE pathway models degrades significantly less than that of random networks when edges are randomly deleted and added, perhaps because of evolutionary pressure to handle changing environments.
claims.quote: The memory capability of biological models is also much more robust to edge perturbation than those of random networks, as indicated in Figure 7, perhaps due to evolutionary pressure to handle changing environments.
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 3. Discussion

claims.label: Pulsatile signalling may let cells behaviour-shape each other in vivo
claims.statement: Because transcriptional and other signalling mechanisms are pulsatile, cells may apply timed behaviour-shaping stimuli to each other in vivo, exploiting the trainability of their pathways to evolve complex phenotypes, though the role of trainability in evolution and development is unknown.
claims.quote: The role of trainability in evolution and development is as yet unknown, but it is interesting that transcriptional [126] and other [127,128] biological signaling mechanisms are now seen as pulsatile, which affords rich opportunity for cells to apply timed “behavior shaping” stimuli to each other in vivo, as a way of exploiting the multiscale competency of biological material to evolve complex phenotypes [129].
claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 3. Discussion

claims.label: Developmental physiology is the control layer between genotype and phenotype
claims.statement: The authors hold that biological genotypes do not code directly for phenotypes; developmental physiology, built from cells with their own context-sensitive behaviours, is the control layer separating genomes from the capacities that selection evaluates.
claims.quote: Biological genotypes do not code directly for phenotypes; developmental physiology is the control layer that separates genomes from capacities ascertained by selection.
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › Abstract

claims.label: Planaria combine a messy mixoploid genome with highly reliable anatomy
claims.statement: Because planaria reproduce by fission and regeneration and so retain somatic mutations, they have a very messy, mixoploid genome, yet they have highly reliable anatomy, with every fragment regenerating a normal worm.
claims.quote: As a result, planaria have an incredibly messy genome (indeed, worms are mixoploid—different numbers of chromosomes in each cell). Despite this, they have the most reliable anatomy: every fragment of a planarian regenerates a perfect worm each time.
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 1. Introduction

claims.label: Cellular competencies come by default, unlike organism-level learning
claims.statement: Unlike organism-level learning, which requires mechanisms such as nervous systems that must themselves be evolved and paid for, cellular competencies come by default because cells already carry capabilities evolved when their ancestors were independent organisms.
claims.quote: In contrast, cellular competencies come “by default” because organisms consist of cellular components that already have many capabilities evolved during their ancestral lifetime as independent organisms.
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 1. Introduction

claims.label: Higher cellular competency accelerates evolutionary search in a 1D embryo model
claims.statement: In a minimal artificial embryogeny model (1D integer arrays whose fitness is their monotonicity, with competent cells performing a restricted bubble sort before fitness evaluation), populations with higher cellular competency reached high fitness faster and more consistently than hardwired populations, e.g. under 6 generations at competency 400 versus over 200 for hardwired.
claims.quote: These data demonstrate the role competency plays in non-linearly improving the rate of fitness of a population and support a clear conclusion: the higher the competency, the better the performance.
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 3. Results › 3.2. Developmental Competency Accelerates Evolutionary Search

test_contract.expected_observation: Pre-registered: with 100 repeats of 250 generations per condition, (a) the generation at which the mean best phenotypic fitness first reaches 1.0 is strictly ordered hardwired > competency 20 > competency 100 > competency 400, and the same weak ordering (>=) holds at every Table 1 threshold (0.65, 0.75, 0.8, 0.9, 0.97, 1.0); (b) competency 400 reaches 1.0 by generation 10 and hardwired does not reach it before generation 100; (c) at generations 2, 10 and 20 each competent population's best phenotypic fitness exceeds hardwired with Welch t-test p < 0.001.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Pre-registered: at the 0.97 or 1.0 threshold some higher competency level is strictly slower than a lower one (including hardwired faster than any competent level), or a competent population is not better than hardwired at generation 10 (p >= 0.05 or lower mean). Outcomes meeting neither the pass nor the fail criterion (ordering holds but the magnitudes in (b) or the significance in (c) are not met) are pre-registered as 'mixed'.
test_contract.inference_method: analysis.py re-implements the model in vectorised numpy without importing the authors' code: per generation it records the best genotypic fitness, develops each embryo by restricted bubble sort, selects the top 10 on phenotypic fitness, refills to 100 by single-point crossover and point-mutates each individual with probability 0.6. Hardwired and competency 20, 100 and 400 populations are each run 100 times for 250 generations from fixed seeds. For each Table 1 threshold it reports the first generation at which the mean best phenotypic fitness reaches it, and runs one-sided Welch t-tests of each competent population against hardwired at generations 2, 10 and 20.

claims.label: Cellular competency reduces selective pressure on structural genes
claims.statement: In the 1D artificial embryogeny model, the genotypic fitness of competent populations rose briefly and then plateaued below that of hardwired populations, with wider variance at higher competency, showing that competency delivers high phenotypic fitness but reduces selective pressure on the structural genes.
claims.quote: Thus, as hypothesized, increasing competency in our simulation enabled excellent performance but reduced selective pressure on the embryo’s structural genes.
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 3. Results › 3.2. Developmental Competency Accelerates Evolutionary Search

test_contract.expected_observation: Competent populations' best genotypic fitness rises for a few generations, then flattens below the hardwired curve, with across-repeat spread increasing with competency level and phenotypic fitness near maximal.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Competent genotypic fitness reaching or exceeding hardwired, continuing to climb, or showing less spread at higher competency.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Runs of the model exactly as specified in the paper and its supplement (50-cell arrays, 100 embryos, top-10% phenotypic selection, crossover, mutation probability 0.6, competency 20/100/400); unspecified details from the authors' public code; fresh random seeds independent of the companion test levin-2023-competency-04.
test_contract.inference_method: Mean curves over 100 repeats; one-sided Welch t-test at generation 250 (alpha 0.001); plateau as window-mean difference < 0.03; spread as mean across-repeat SD over generations 51-250 compared across levels.

claims.label: Competent embryos take over mixed populations given enough competency or numbers
claims.statement: In mixed populations of the 1D artificial embryogeny model, competent embryos starting as a minority came to dominate hardwired ones within two or three generations, and the competency needed to dominate fell as their initial share rose (75 at 10%, 40 at 20%, 10 at 30%), while at 2.5% they did not dominate even at competency 95.
claims.quote: As their initial proportion in the population increased, competent embryos required progressively less competency to dominate over their hardwired competitors.
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 3. Results › 3.3. Competent Individuals Take over Mixed Populations

test_contract.expected_observation: A dominance threshold in competency that decreases with initial competent share near 75/40/10 at 10/20/30%, no dominance at 2.5% up to competency 95, and rapid (<= 3 generation) takeover where dominance occurs.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Thresholds that do not fall with share or sit far (> 40 swaps) from the reported values, or clear dominance at 2.5%.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Runs of the mixed-population model as described in the paper (200 embryos, competent minority, top-10% selection on phenotypic fitness for competent and genotypic for hardwired embryos, crossover, mutation probability 0.6), with heritable type labels; unspecified details from the authors' public code.
test_contract.inference_method: Mean competent share over 50 repeats per condition at generation 20 compared with 0.5 to define dominance; threshold c* read off a 5-swap competency grid and compared with the claimed values with a +/-20 tolerance; takeover time from the mean share curve.

claims.label: Evolvable competency rises rapidly and plateaus at a high level
claims.statement: In the 1D artificial embryogeny model, when competency is set by an evolvable gene (range 1–500, initialized at 1–15), the best individual's competency rose rapidly and plateaued around 470, higher than the roughly 364 needed for maximum fitness, a level the authors attribute to random drift among equally fit values.
claims.quote: The prevalence of the competency allele rapidly rose, meandering and exploring values up to 485 during evolution (shaded area in Figure 5A) before plateauing at ~470.
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 3. Results › 3.4. Evolution Results in a High, Constant Level of Competency

test_contract.expected_observation: Best-individual competency climbing from <= 15 to a stable plateau near 470 within the first tens of generations, above the inversion count of its genome.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: A plateau well below 470 (< 400), at or below the needed competency, or no rise.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Runs of the evolvable-competency model as described in the paper (competency gene range [1, 500], initial [1, 15], 1000 generations, top-10% phenotypic selection, crossover, mutation probability 0.6), with unspecified details from the authors' public code.
test_contract.inference_method: Mean over 30 repeats of the per-generation best-individual competency; plateau as the generation 801-1000 mean compared with the [440, 500] band and with the mean inversion count; rise time as first generation >= 300.

claims.label: Evolvable competency decouples genotypic from phenotypic fitness
claims.statement: In the 1D artificial embryogeny model with evolvable competency, the correlation between genotypic and phenotypic fitness fell to zero within about 20 generations, so allowing competency to evolve disrupts selection's ability to pick the best structural genes.
claims.quote: Correlation dropped to 0 within about 20 generations as individuals who succeeded because of their developmental competencies rapidly dominated the population. We conclude that allowing competency to evolve disrupts the ability to select for the best structural genes.
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 3. Results › 3.4. Evolution Results in a High, Constant Level of Competency

test_contract.expected_observation: Across-individual genotype-phenotype fitness correlation near 1 at the start, ~0 from about generation 20 onward.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: A substantial positive correlation (>= 0.3) persisting after generation 20.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Runs of the evolvable-competency model as described in the paper, with unspecified details from the authors' public code; seeds independent of the levin-2023-competency-07 test.
test_contract.inference_method: Per-generation across-individual Pearson r averaged over 30 repeats, window means over generations 21-40 and 41-1000 compared with thresholds 0.1 (pass) and 0.3 (fail).

claims.label: A cost on competency restores a Baldwin effect and genetic assimilation
claims.statement: In the 1D artificial embryogeny model, penalizing fitness in proportion to competency (penalty factors 1×10⁻⁷ to 0.5) produced a Baldwin effect: structural-gene fitness kept improving, selection favoured progressively lower competency, and early competency-based gains were assimilated into the structural genes; the authors note real competency costs are unmeasured.
claims.quote: Thus early gains based on the competency gene are later assimilated into the structural genes, paralleling what has been described previously in the context of organism-level learning [59].
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 3. Results › 3.5. A Fitness Penalty for Competency Leads to Continued Improvement of an Embryo’s Structural Genes

claims.label: Planaria are an example of runaway cellular competency
claims.statement: The authors propose that planaria exemplify runaway competency: their cells became so good at compensating for structural-gene deficiencies that selection could no longer pick the best genomes, so evolution instead increased generic competency to reach the target morphology, explaining a chaotic genome with robust anatomy.
claims.quote: We propose that planaria are an example of runaway competency: when cells get really good at making up for deficiencies in the structural genes, evolution has such a hard time selecting for the best genomes that further improvements instead increase generic competency to reach their target morphology despite perturbations.
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 4. Discussion › 4.4. The Paradox of Robustness: Why the Animal with the Worst Genome Has the Best Anatomy

claims.label: Planaria lack morphological mutant lines; the only abnormal line is bioelectric
claims.statement: Unlike other model species, planaria have no reported morphologically abnormal genetic strains; the only abnormal line is a permanently two-headed form produced by manipulating bioelectric signalling rather than genes, which the authors say is predicted by their model for species like planaria.
claims.quote: In planaria this does not exist—no morphologically abnormal genetic strains have been reported. In fact, the only available abnormal line of planaria is a permanently two-headed form [96,97,98], which was produced not genetically but by manipulating bioelectrical signaling—the modality that is used to coordinate cellular competency [99,100,101], as is predicted by our model for species like planaria.
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 4. Discussion › 4.4. The Paradox of Robustness: Why the Animal with the Worst Genome Has the Best Anatomy

claims.label: Evolution changes the competency gene more often than any structural gene
claims.statement: In the 1D artificial embryogeny model with evolvable competency, positional changes to cells over 1000 generations resulted from changes to the competency gene significantly more often than from changes to any of the fifty structural genes.
claims.quote: We found that the competency gene is changed significantly more often over the course of evolution than any structural gene (Figure 6).
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 4. Discussion › 4.6. Where the Hard Work Is Done: An Intelligence Ratchet

claims.label: An intelligence ratchet locks evolution into improving cellular competency
claims.statement: The authors suggest that because competency hides genetic deficiencies from selection, a positive-feedback ratchet arises in which evolution increasingly improves the problem-solving competency (intelligence) of its cellular material rather than the structural genome, a possible driver for scaling intelligence in morphological and other spaces.
claims.quote: This suggests the existence of a powerful ratchet mechanism in which evolution progressively becomes locked into improvements in the intelligence of the agential material with which it works, with reduced pressure on the structural genes.
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 4. Discussion › 4.6. Where the Hard Work Is Done: An Intelligence Ratchet

claims.label: Problem-solving competency drove evolution long before brains
claims.statement: The authors suggest that intelligence, understood as problem-solving competency, was an evolutionary driver long before complex brains and muscle-driven behaviour arose, so basal cognition is an important part of evolutionary developmental biology.
claims.quote: and that intelligence (problem-solving competency) was an evolutionary driver long before complex brains and muscle-driven behavior arose [52,53,56,136,137,138,139,140,141,142,143].
claims.work: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model
claims.chapter: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 5. Conclusions

claims.label: Evolution scales cell-level metabolic homeostasis into a tissue-level French flag axis
claims.statement: In a 2D neural cellular automaton in which each cell only pursues metabolic (energy) homeostasis and is rewarded according to how well its stripe matches the pattern, evolution (ES-HyperNEAT) produced cell collectives with tissue-level setpoints that solve the French flag problem, i.e. organize a body-wide three-valued positional information axis.
claims.quote: Our system showed the evolution of the much more complex setpoints of cell collectives (tissues) that solve a problem in morphospace: the organization of a body-wide positional information axis (the classic French flag problem in developmental biology).
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Abstract

claims.label: Robust patterning works best from a homogeneous starting state
claims.statement: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, French flag patterning works less well from random initial cell states, suggesting that robust development is optimized when cells start from a homogeneous undifferentiated baseline, as real embryos do.
claims.quote: It seems to work less well with random initializations, suggesting that robust development is optimized when cells start with a muted, homogeneous ‘baseline’ state, not highly diverse starting states, which is indeed what is observed in real development
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › The tissue minimizes error for reaching the target morphology

claims.label: Evolved tissues repair perturbed patterns although repair was never selected for
claims.statement: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, tissues selected only to self-organize the French flag within 100 steps could restore the target pattern after perturbations applied later (e.g. converting two columns of the red stripe to white at step 110), although they failed after very large perturbations such as converting the whole red stripe.
claims.quote: Thus, we conclude that even though we did not specifically reward for anything other than the single self-organizing property, the cells were able to repair to the target setpoint from multiple starting configurations.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › The tissue is robust to perturbation

claims.label: Stress spikes precede spontaneous late remodelling in the simulated tissue
claims.statement: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, the tissue spontaneously remodels long after its pattern has stabilized, without external perturbation, and a sharp spike in stress immediately precedes each onset of morphogenetic activity, suggesting that stress drives the morphogenetic changes.
claims.quote: In our simulations, a dramatic spike in stress immediately precedes the sharp onset of extensive morphogenetic activity (see electronic supplementary material, figure S1a), suggesting that stress drives the morphogenetic changes in the tissue.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › The tissue maintains allostasis in adulthood

claims.label: Long-term tissue stability emerges without selection for it
claims.statement: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, tissues evolved only over 100-step development maintained their pattern for 1000 steps (allostasis), showing that in this model long-term stable survival need not be selected for because intrinsic dynamics and emergent regenerative capacity maintain order in an adult phase.
claims.quote: Thus, we conclude that long-term stable survival does not need to be specifically selected for, as intrinsic dynamics and emergent anatomical regenerative capacity are enough to maintain order through an adult phase.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › The tissue maintains allostasis in adulthood

claims.label: Blocking stress signalling prevents anatomical homeostasis in a stress-using tissue
claims.statement: In an evolved neural cellular automaton tissue that uses stress as an instructive signal, forcing stress to zero throughout life (a simulated anxiolytic) lowered pattern accuracy (82.8% vs 95.1% at step 90) and killed the red-stripe cells, so anatomical homeostasis was neither reached nor maintained.
claims.quote: These experiments reveal that, in the absence of stress, anatomical homeostasis is not reached nor maintained during the lifetime of the cells.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Evolution exploits stress as an instructive signal to reach the target morphology

claims.label: Evolved stress signalling is instructive only at specific concentrations
claims.statement: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, imposing very high stress on an already patterned tissue had no immediate effect on cell states but later altered them, indicating that evolution used stress as a communication code in which stress affects cell behaviour only at specific concentrations.
claims.quote: We conclude that evolution used stress as a communication system using a particular encoding, in which stress level is instructive and has effects on cell behaviour only at specific concentrations.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Stress is instructive but only at particular levels

claims.label: Stress propagation is not required for patterning but improves adaptation to change
claims.statement: Across 10 evolved neural cellular automaton tissues, stress signalling was not required to solve the French flag problem (only 1 of 10 died without it), but the tissue that used stress instructively scored significantly better when the target morphology was changed mid-development (p = 0.0312), suggesting that spatial propagation of stress information increases adaptive fitness under perturbation.
claims.quote: For this problem, anatomical homeostasis without stress is possible but exploiting spatial propagation of stress information seems to increase adaptive fitness by improving performance in scenarios where the normal process of morphogenesis is impacted by external perturbations.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Evolution exploits the stress system but anxiolytics do not always have an impact on anatomical homeostasis

claims.label: Evolved stress signalling acts paracrine rather than autocrine
claims.statement: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, transfer entropy from a cell's stress to its neighbours' states is much larger than to its own state, suggesting that the key signalling mode of stress is paracrine, not autocrine.
claims.quote: We also compared the transfer entropy from stress of one cell to its own state and found it to be much less important than the transfer entropy from the stress of one cell to the states of its neighbours (figure 8c). This suggests the key signalling mode for the stress is paracrine, not autocrine.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis

claims.label: Simulated embryonic regions take turns acting as the organizer
claims.statement: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, transfer entropy between stripes first flows mainly from the red to the white stripe and then reverses, suggesting that the 'organizer' region (a group of cells that instructively patterns others) changes over time and embryonic regions take turns driving large-scale patterning.
claims.quote: The ‘organizer’ region (here defined as a region or group of cells in a tissue that can induce and instructively pattern other cells) seemed to change over time, suggesting embryonic regions take turns driving the large-scale process.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis

claims.label: Information flows first from the anatomical loop to single-cell energy
claims.statement: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, transfer entropy from energy to cell state peaks before the reverse flow, indicating that information is first driven by the tissue-level anatomical homeostatic loop, which then controls the energy cells need to survive; the authors take this to suggest top-down information is key to manipulating tissue dynamics.
claims.quote: Thus, in our scheme, the information was first driven by the anatomical loop, and the energy needed for single-cell survival was controlled by this loop.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis

claims.label: Stress rises when cellular memory fails to predict the future
claims.statement: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, stress increases concurrently with a fall in local active information storage of cell states, so evolution used the stress system as a communication channel activated when memory of past events does not predict the future, matching the definition of stressors as unpredictable or uncontrollable stimuli.
claims.quote: In our scheme, evolution used the stress system as a communication system that was activated when memory of past events was not effective for predicting the future.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
claims.chapter: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis

claims.label: Model predicts sudden late remodelling of apparently stable biological patterns
claims.statement: Because the neural cellular automaton suddenly remodelled cell fates after a long period of quiescent, stable pattern, the authors predict that something similar may occur in biological systems: some phenotypes that appear complete may need to be followed much longer to see their true dynamics.
claims.quote: The sudden remodelling of cell fates after a long period of apparently quiescent, stable pattern in our model (figure 4) predicts that something similar may occur in biological systems.
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

claims.label: 22% of headless ERK-inhibited planaria spontaneously repattern weeks later
claims.statement: In Dugesia japonica made headless by transient U0126 (ERK/MAP kinase inhibitor) treatment after amputation, 22% of 181 animals followed until death showed sudden repatterning after four or more weeks without any intervention, mostly between 4 and 10 weeks, and 61% of those regained a normal single-headed morphology.
claims.quote: In headless animals observed from when they were cut until their death (n = 181), 22% showed some form of sudden repatterning even though regeneration had completed and morphogenesis had ceased weeks prior (figure 10b).
claims.work: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis
